allocation.description: How the effect is applied across the matched items or charges. each applies the effect to every matched item independently: a fixed amount_off is charged per item (10 USD off 3 items discounts 30 USD, each capped at the item price), and a percent_off is taken from each item. across applies the effect once to the matched set as a whole: a fixed amount_off is the whole amount one time (10 USD off the group total, not prorated per item), and a percent_off is taken from the combined subtotal. For percent_off the two produce the same total and differ only in how the discount is attributed to individual line items; for amount_off they differ by the number of matched items, so set it deliberately. Defaults to each for line_item and service_charge promotions and across for order promotions. max_discounted_quantity requires each.

Flint rejects an input or calculation above this ceiling with INVALID_REQUEST and detail INVALID_VALUE at the responsible input field. Lower payment option limits can apply.

promotion_id.description: Use `promotion_id` for server-side apply flows where you already know the promotion, including code-gated promotions, which then apply without a code and count only toward the promotion's `max_uses`. Checkout credentials must use `promotion_code`. Fixed promotion amounts applied to orders must satisfy the order money ceiling. The amount and every computed order amount must not exceed 99999999 minor units ($999,999.99 USD). Flint rejects an input or calculation above this ceiling with INVALID_REQUEST and detail INVALID_VALUE at the responsible input field. Lower payment option limits can apply.

PromotionRule.description: One condition in a promotion rule group, which tests an attribute with an operator and values.

attribute.description: Field the rule tests. The attribute fixes the value type and the operators that are legal for it: money attributes accept comparison operators but not eq or in, booleans accept eq only, and so on. The full attribute/type/operator matrix is machine-readable in x-flint-rule-attributes on this schema. metadata.<key> reads a string from the customer's metadata and accepts the string operators. A disallowed operator returns `400 INVALID_REQUEST` naming the operator, and the message lists the operators the attribute allows.

currency_options.description: Alternative thresholds for money-valued rules, keyed by currency code. Each Money currency must match its key.

operator.description: Comparison to apply to the attribute. The attribute determines which operators are allowed.

PromotionRuleGroup.description: A rule group is an object with exactly one nonempty all (AND) or any (OR) array of rules or nested groups. Arrays, empty groups, and a rules key are invalid. Omit the field for no rules, or send null where the field is clearable. Responses list rules before nested groups. Under any, a nested group containing only one rule reads back as that rule. Under all, nested groups keep their boundaries to preserve matched_items.subtotal scope. These deterministic normalizations stabilize after one round trip. matched_items.subtotal sums the line items matched by the line_item.* rules in the same all group, including its nested groups.

timezone.description: IANA zone the schedule was entered in, used for display. starts_at and ends_at are absolute timestamps, so this does not change when the promotion starts or ends.

PromotionSettings.description: Merchant promotion settings: whether automatic promotions and codes are enabled, and how many promotions can apply to one order.

automatic_enabled.description: Whether automatic promotions apply to this merchant's orders, checkout sessions and payment links. Omitted means true. Explicit false stops them everywhere, and a checkout session or payment link can't turn them back on.

codes_enabled.description: Merchant promotion code redemption policy. Explicit false rejects promotion-code application even when a checkout or payment link asks to show code entry.

max_promotions_per_order.description: Maximum promotion discounts on an order, from 1 to 10, default 2. Manual discounts do not count. See Promotion for the evaluation order.

PublicDownload.description: A temporary link for downloading a generated report.

expires_at.description: When the download stops working: 24 hours after the report succeeded. The report keeps status succeeded and this download object afterward; create a new report to get the file again.

report_download_id.description: Identifier of this download, the last segment of url.

url.description: Flint API URL for the file, not the file itself. Call it with the same API key; Flint answers 307 with a redirect to a private file URL that works for a few minutes. Request url again each time you need the file.

PublicPaymentLink.description: The buyer-facing view of a payment link, with its line items, custom fields, legal and payment settings, and status.

completed_count.description: Number of paid checkout sessions started from this link.

custom_fields.description: Questions buyers answer before paying. Answers are saved in order metadata as `custom_field_<key>`.

custom_text.description: Custom text for checkouts started from this link.

description.description: Text about what the link sells, returned to buyers when they open it.

donation_max_amount_money.description: Largest amount a buyer can give on a donation link.

donation_min_amount_money.description: Smallest amount a buyer can give on a donation link.

donation_suggested_amount_money_options.description: Amounts a donation link offers as one-tap choices.

event_config.description: Event details for an `event` link: when and where it takes place and how many tickets it sells.

image.description: Image shown to buyers with the link.

inactive_message.description: Message to show the buyer when the link is inactive.

legal.description: The terms and policy links checkouts started from this link show the buyer.

line_items.description: What the link sells.

max_completions.description: Most payments the link accepts, counted by `completed_count`. Absent means no limit. Once the limit is reached, resolving the link fails with a request error. It can't be set below `completed_count`.

name.description: Name of the payment link.

payment_link_type.description: What kind of link this is.
x-enum-descriptions: Sells the link's line items at their configured prices.
The buyer chooses how much to give, within the donation limits and suggested amounts.
Sells tickets to the event in `event_config`.

payments.description: Payment options for checkouts started from this link.

sales_end_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp after which the link stops starting checkouts and resolve fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `not_offered`. Unset means sales do not end on their own, except that an event link without sales_end_at stops selling at event_config.event_at. A checkout opened before the end can still start payment for up to 15 minutes after it.

status.description: Whether the link can start new checkouts.
x-enum-descriptions: Buyers can open the link and start a checkout.
The link starts no checkouts. Resolving it fails; show `inactive_message` to the buyer.

subscription_plan_id.description: ID of the subscription plan the link sells.

theme.description: The title and colors for checkouts started from this link, over your branding settings.

version.description: Current version of this resource's owned state. Send it as `expected_version` when changing the resource to reject a stale write.

data.description: Resource, collection, or operation result returned by this request.

request_id.description: Identifier of this API request, used to correlate logs and support requests.

PublicPaymentLinkResult.description: The result of resolving a public payment link: the link, merchant branding, availability, resolved line items, and a resolution context for starting checkout.

checkout_theme.description: The theme a checkout opened from this link uses: your checkout branding settings, with the link's own `theme` over them. Use it to style a page that leads to the checkout. `payment_link.theme` is the link's own theme alone. Omitted when neither sets a value. It includes the branding settings' `background_color`, `text_color`, `font_family`, and `corner_radius`.

is_sold_out.description: True for an event with no tickets remaining. For other active links with inventory_routing_source, true when any catalog line cannot be bought at its minimum quantity from that source. Untracked and ad hoc lines do not count. A choice line counts only when every offered variant is sold out. Fixed locations use available stock; policies use their allocatable locations. Stock is not reserved by this read.

payment_link.description: The payment link that was resolved.

remaining_quantity.description: Event links with a ticket limit: tickets left after tickets sold and tickets held by payments in progress. Absent when the event has no ticket limit. Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

resolution_context.description: The context checkout needs to start from this result.

resolved_line_items.description: The link's line items with their current catalog values.

sales_ended.description: True when the link's sales end has passed: payment_link.sales_end_at, or event_config.event_at for an event link without sales_end_at. Resolve then fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `not_offered`.

show_flint_mark.description: Whether Flint's hosted pages show the Powered by Flint mark for this merchant. `false` when the merchant's agreement with Flint removes it.

subscription_preview.description: Present for active plan-backed payment links when authoritative subscription terms are available.

available_variants.description: Listed variants that can currently be sold in the line currency, in variant_ids order. Inactive, archived, unsellable, and other-currency variants are omitted. Each variant includes its advisory sold-out state and its own modifiers. Present only on variant_ids lines.

bundle_components.description: The components of the bundle. Present for a bundle line item.

bundle_id.description: ID of the bundle this line item sells.

A bundle of items sold together.

is_inventory_tracked.description: Whether Flint tracks stock for the item.

is_sold_out.description: True when the fixed variant or bundle components cannot be bought at the line minimum quantity from the link inventory_routing_source. The minimum is min_quantity when quantity adjustment is enabled, otherwise quantity. For variant choice lines, true only when every available_variants entry is sold out. Always false for untracked and ad hoc lines. Exposes no stock counts and reserves no stock.

key.description: Key of the payment link line item this entry describes.

product_id.description: ID of the product the variant belongs to.

The merchant pays the overdue amount owed to Flint.

Only Flint support can clear this.

A call your integration makes.

x-enum-descriptions: Works now. `next_actions` can still offer an account session when information will be due later.
Waiting: Flint is preparing the sandbox (`provisioning`), verification hasn't been submitted (`onboarding_not_started`), or submitted information is under review (`pending_verification`).
Something must be resolved first. `status_reason` says what and `next_actions` says who acts.
The account never requested this capability.
Flint couldn't read readiness. Read the merchant again later.

status_reason.description: Why readiness has its current status. MERCHANT_NOT_READY uses onboarding_required for onboarding_not_started, requirements_due, requirements_past_due and pending_verification, and platform_review for Flint's own review. `null` when no reason applies.
x-enum-descriptions: Flint is automatically preparing this sandbox to accept test payments. No action is required; read readiness again shortly.
Account verification hasn't been submitted.
Information in `requirements.currently_due` is due. Collect it with a merchant account session or on the dashboard.
Information in `requirements.past_due` missed its deadline. Collect it with a merchant account session or on the dashboard.
Submitted information is under review. Nothing to do.
The account was rejected; `requirements.rejected_by` says by whom. Contact Flint support.
Flint or the payment processor suspended, closed or restricted the account. Contact Flint support.
Flint paused processing because an amount owed to Flint is overdue. Paying it resumes processing.
Flint paused processing while it reviews the account. Contact Flint support.
Flint hasn't turned on processing for this account. Contact Flint support.
Payments or payouts are temporarily unavailable on Flint's platform. Nothing on the account caused it.
Live payments and payouts are paused until the merchant chooses a supported automatic tax category.
Flint couldn't read readiness, or processing is temporarily unavailable. Read again later.
The payment option isn't set up for this account. Contact Flint support.
Flint is still activating the payment option.
The merchant's Flint plan doesn't include the payment option.
The payment option isn't available for this account.
The capability isn't active on the account. Contact Flint support.
A reason without a published name. Follow `next_actions`.

Collects only what is due now.

future_requirements.description: Whether onboarding also collects requirements the processor has scheduled for a future date. include collects them now; omit leaves them until they are due.
x-enum-descriptions: Future requirements are not collected.
Future requirements are collected too.

targeted_requirements.description: Flint requirement codes. New codes can appear; treat an unknown code as additional_account_information.

Required information is missing.

Refund.description: Money returned against a collected payment.

customer.description: Present only when `expand` includes `customer`; `null` when expanded and there is no related customer.

external_reference_id.description: Caller-owned identifier for this resource in an external system.

failure_reason.description: Why a refund failed or a payment refund was canceled. Failed and canceled amounts become refundable again. Fix the cause, then create a new refund with a new idempotency key. Unknown provider values are returned as refund_failed.
x-enum-descriptions: The card can no longer receive credits.
The card was reported lost or stolen.
The refund could not be funded.
Your available balance could not cover the refund.
The card issuer declined the credit.
The refund was stopped at the merchant's request.
The payment is under dispute, or a bank return took the money back first. The buyer already has it through their bank.
On partially_succeeded: one or more payment refunds failed. Read payment_refunds.
This payment refund was canceled before it was attempted because another payment refund failed.
The refund failed with no more specific reason.

idempotency_key.description: Present only on refunds created through POST /v1/credit-notes/{credit_note_id}/refunds or by issuing a credit note with refund: the Idempotency-Key of that call. Use it with GET /v1/credit-notes/{credit_note_id}/refunds?idempotency_key= to recover a refund whose create response was lost.

merchant_id.description: ID of the merchant this resource belongs to.

metadata.description: Stored caller-owned key-value data. See `MetadataInput` for key, value, and size rules.

order.description: Present only when `expand` includes `order`; `null` when expanded and there is no related order.

payment_intent.description: Present only when `expand` includes `payment_intent`; `null` when expanded and there is no related payment intent.

refund_id.description: Unique identifier for this refund, prefixed `ref_`.

status.description: Summary of payment_refunds and tender_allocations. Only failed is final: succeeded and partially_succeeded can still change when a bank rejects a refund after accepting it. Follow refund.updated.
x-enum-descriptions: At least one payment refund or tender allocation is still in progress.
Every payment refund and tender allocation succeeded. Can still become partially_succeeded or failed after a bank rejection.
Some payment refunds or tender allocations succeeded and the rest failed or were canceled. failure_reason is payment_refund_failed. Can still become failed.
No money went back. failure_reason says why. The amount is refundable again. This status is final.

unissued_gift_card_recoveries.description: Cash returned after an unissued gift card purchase refund failed. Return it through a new refund against payment_intent_id and order_line_item_id. It does not issue another card. Source remaining and pending amounts describe the entire original settlement allocation; repeated entries for that source are not additive.

version.description: Persisted version of this resource's owned state. Expanded resources and external observations can change independently.

RefundAdjustmentAudit.description: Who made a manual tax adjustment on a refund line item and where it came from, for audit purposes.

RefundAdjustmentReasonInput.description: The reason to record for a refund adjustment, as a `code` with an optional description.

RefundCharge.description: An order charge to refund when creating a refund, with an optional amount to refund.

RefundDestinations.description: Default refund destinations for payment intent and gift card redemption allocations planned by Flint. Each tender type defaults to original when omitted.

gift_card_redemption.description: Where gift card redemption value is refunded. original credits the original gift card; new_gift_card issues new gift cards, including when the original is closed or cannot accept the full credit.

payment_intent.description: Default destination for every payment intent allocation Flint plans for this refund. original returns value to the payment; new_gift_card issues store credit on new Flint gift cards. Payment intent store credit requires a succeeded USD card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, or Link payment that belongs to an order, with no open chargeback. Affirm, ACH debit, other payment options, non-USD payments, and payments without an order return INVALID_REQUEST with a NOT_ALLOWED detail. Payment chargebacks use the existing dispute refusal. Gift card redemption destinations are unaffected by the payment restrictions.

RefundGiftCardCode.description: The code of a gift card issued by a refund, returned once in the refund result with its `gift_card_id`.

RefundGiftCardDestination.description: A gift card that received part of a refund, with the amount credited.

RefundLineItem.description: An order line item to refund, with the quantity or amount, tax handling, and any adjustments such as a restocking fee.

quantity.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

ResourceVersionRequest.description: The request body for: Mark invoice uncollectible; Regenerate invoice public link; Resume one of the current buyer's subscriptions; Resume subscription; Reverse credit note allocation; Void credit note; Void invoice.

expected_version.description: Version last read from the resource returned in `data` (the primary resource for a result object). The write fails with `VERSION_CONFLICT` if it has changed. Requiredness depends on the operation and fields being changed.

ResponseMeta.description: Metadata returned with a response: the `api_version`, `trace_id`, whether an idempotent request was replayed, and any warnings.

api_version.description: API version used to produce this response.

idempotency_replayed.description: Whether this response replays a stored result for the supplied Idempotency-Key.

trace_id.description: Trace identifier to include when contacting Flint about this request.

warnings.description: Conditions that need attention even though the request succeeded.

ResponseWarning.description: A non-blocking condition reported with a response. The `code` identifies the condition and `severity` says how urgent it is.

due_at.description: Time by which the merchant must submit onboarding requirements, as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp. Present only for merchant_onboarding_deadline or merchant_onboarding_past_due when a submission deadline is set. Allowed for `merchant_onboarding_past_due`, `merchant_onboarding_deadline` warnings.

next_actions.description: Suggested actions for addressing the warning. Allowed for `merchant_onboarding_past_due`, `merchant_onboarding_deadline`, `merchant_capability_pending`, `merchant_capability_inactive`, `payout_settings_reconciling` warnings.

observed_at.description: Last synchronization time for merchant_onboarding_past_due, merchant_onboarding_deadline, merchant_capability_pending, or merchant_capability_inactive, when available. Allowed for `merchant_onboarding_past_due`, `merchant_onboarding_deadline`, `merchant_capability_pending`, `merchant_capability_inactive` warnings.

previous_stage.description: Previous risk rule evaluation stage for rule_evaluation_stage_changed. Allowed for `rule_evaluation_stage_changed` warnings.

promotion_code.description: Promotion code that was accepted but did not apply, on a promotion_declined warning, or the code of a removed promotion discount, on a promotion_removed warning. Allowed for `promotion_declined`, `promotion_removed` warnings.

reason.description: Stable Flint reason code. On a promotion_declined or promotion_removed warning this is the promotion decline reason (for example superseded_by_better_offer); an unrecognized value falls back to not_eligible. See the Promotions reference for the full list. Allowed for `promotion_declined`, `promotion_removed` warnings.

ReturnLineDecision.description: Start from the pinned policy proposal recomputed for approved_quantity when the line has a policy evaluation and the proposal can be built. Otherwise start with return_required_quantity equal to approved_quantity, allowed_resolution_types containing refund, exchange, replacement, no_monetary_action, and store_credit in that order regardless of whether the original payment is refundable, no automatic_resolution_type, is_inspection_required false, and no receiving_location_id. Each supplied field replaces its starting value; allowed_resolution_types replaces the whole list. Omit automatic_resolution_type to keep its starting value, or send null to resolve manually. Then fill an omitted release_timing with after_inspection when merchandise is required and inspection is required, after_receipt when merchandise is required without inspection, or after_approval when no merchandise is required. Validate the merged decision for quantity bounds, allowed resolution types, and reachable timing and inspection requirements. A pinned policy always requires override_reason when approved_quantity exceeds evaluated eligible_quantity, even when no proposal can be built. With a pinned policy but no proposal, other decision fields use these defaults and override_reason is otherwise optional.

allowed_resolution_types.description: Optional replacement for the entire starting list. Defaults to the buildable pinned policy proposal; otherwise refund, exchange, replacement, no_monetary_action, and store_credit in that order, independent of the original payment's refundability. The resulting list must be valid and non-empty when approved_quantity is above zero.

approved_quantity.description: Required whole-number quantity from zero through the line's requested_quantity; fractional quantities are not supported. When approved_quantity is below requested_quantity, send decline_reason; decline_reason_message is optional. Both decline fields are forbidden when all requested quantity is approved.

automatic_resolution_type.description: Optional refund, store_credit, or no_monetary_action that Flint creates and confirms automatically. Omit to keep the policy proposal's value, or the absent value from no-policy defaults. Send null to resolve the line manually; clearing a policy proposal's automatic value requires override_reason. Must be in the resulting allowed_resolution_types. Exchange and replacement cannot be automated. An unavailable automatic refund or store credit fails with 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED and reason refund_unavailable or store_credit_unavailable.

ReturnProcessDecision.description: Start from the pinned policy proposal recomputed for approved_quantity when the line has a policy evaluation and the proposal can be built. Otherwise start with return_required_quantity equal to approved_quantity, allowed_resolution_types containing refund, exchange, replacement, no_monetary_action, and store_credit in that order regardless of whether the original payment is refundable, no automatic_resolution_type, is_inspection_required false, and no receiving_location_id. Each supplied field replaces its starting value; allowed_resolution_types replaces the whole list. Omit automatic_resolution_type to keep its starting value, or send null to resolve manually. Then fill an omitted release_timing with after_inspection when merchandise is required and inspection is required, after_receipt when merchandise is required without inspection, or after_approval when no merchandise is required. Validate the merged decision for quantity bounds, allowed resolution types, and reachable timing and inspection requirements. A pinned policy always requires override_reason when approved_quantity exceeds evaluated eligible_quantity, even when no proposal can be built. With a pinned policy but no proposal, other decision fields use these defaults and override_reason is otherwise optional.

allowed_resolution_types.description: Optional replacement for the entire starting list. Defaults to the buildable pinned policy proposal; otherwise refund, exchange, replacement, no_monetary_action, and store_credit in that order, independent of the original payment's refundability. The resulting list must be valid and non-empty when approved_quantity is above zero.

x-enum-descriptions: Money back to the original payment, with gift card value sent to the chosen gift card destination.
Different merchandise; the buyer may owe or be owed the difference.
The same merchandise again, with no money moving.
Nothing is owed either way.
Refunds the returned value onto new gift cards instead of the original payment. Card, wallet and Link payments and gift cards qualify; Affirm and ACH debit payments do not.

approved_quantity.description: Required whole-number quantity from zero through the line's requested_quantity; fractional quantities are not supported. When approved_quantity is below requested_quantity, send decline_reason; decline_reason_message is optional. Both decline fields are forbidden when all requested quantity is approved.

automatic_resolution_type.description: Optional refund, store_credit, or no_monetary_action that Flint creates and confirms automatically. Omit to keep the policy proposal's value, or the absent value from no-policy defaults. Send null to resolve the line manually; clearing a policy proposal's automatic value requires override_reason. Must be in the resulting allowed_resolution_types. Exchange and replacement cannot be automated. An unavailable automatic refund or store credit fails with 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED and reason refund_unavailable or store_credit_unavailable.
x-enum-descriptions: Money back to the original payment, with gift card value sent to the chosen gift card destination.
Refunds the returned value onto new gift cards instead of the original payment. Card, wallet and Link payments and gift cards qualify; Affirm and ACH debit payments do not.
Nothing is owed either way.
Flint creates no resolution on its own. You resolve the line yourself.

decline_reason.description: Why the line's declined quantity is declined.
x-enum-descriptions: The line doesn't qualify under the return policy.
Less than the requested quantity remains returnable.
The evidence the return policy requires is missing.
Abuse of the return policy is suspected.
The merchant decided, without a policy reason.
A reason the other values don't cover.

decline_reason_message.description: Optional explanation accompanying decline_reason, up to 2048 characters (Unicode code points), counted before normalization. Requires decline_reason and is forbidden when all requested quantity is approved.

is_inspection_required.description: Optional inspection requirement. Defaults to the buildable pinned policy proposal or false when no proposal can be built. The resulting requirement must be reachable with the merged merchandise quantity and release timing.

override_reason.description: Required when a decision differs from a buildable pinned policy proposal. SelectableOrderPaymentIntent.description: A payment intent on an order the caller can pick, with its amount, status, and last payment error.

amount_money.description: The amount requested from the buyer, including any tip_money. Capturing doesn't change it: after a partial capture it still shows the requested amount, and captured_money shows what was collected. On a standalone payment intent, PATCH can change it only before the first confirmation attempt.

last_payment_error.description: Most recent payment failure, when one is recorded.

payment_collection.description: Client setup details for collecting this payment.

payment_intent_id.description: Flint payment intent ID.

status.description: Lifecycle status. requires_payment_method covers both a new payment intent and one whose last attempt failed, so read last_payment_error with it. succeeded, canceled, and expired are final. Refunds and disputes never change status.
x-enum-descriptions: Waiting for the buyer's payment details. Either nothing has been attempted yet, or the last attempt was declined, failed, or blocked and last_payment_error says why. Confirm again with a new credential.

Payment details are attached, but confirmation hasn't finished. Flint usually confirms in the same request that attaches them, so this status is brief unless that confirmation was interrupted. Resume the order's payment attempt, or call confirm with credential_type attached for a standalone payment intent. The payment_intent.updated event reports changes into this status.

The buyer must finish a step, such as 3D Secure authentication or a redirect, before the payment can continue. The confirm result's current_payment_action describes a standalone payment's step; call confirm with credential_type attached to retrieve it again. Afterward, call confirm with credential_type attached, or resume the order's payment attempt.

Submitted, with the outcome not known yet. ACH debit payments stay here until the bank settles them, which takes a few business days. Card payments pass through briefly. A processing payment intent can't be canceled or updated.
A manual-capture hold is in place and no money has been collected. Capture up to capturable_money, or cancel, before authorization_expires_at.

Canceled before any money was collected, by you or by Flint, for example when an invoice is voided. Final. cancellation_reason says why when Flint knows it. A canceled hold is in released_money. This status is final.
The payment is collected, and captured_money is the amount. Final. This status is final.

A manual-capture hold reached authorization_expires_at without a capture, and the funds went back to the buyer. Final. The payment_intent.expired event reports it; cancellation_reason is absent. This status is final.

branding.description: Colors, font, and corner radius of hosted checkout, receipts, and links. Omitted until you save a value in this section; effective settings fill in Flint's defaults.

checkout.description: Defaults for hosted checkout. Omitted until you save a value in this section; effective settings fill in Flint's defaults.

customer_account.description: The customer account where buyers manage their orders, subscriptions, returns, and invoices. Omitted until you save a value in this section; effective settings fill in Flint's defaults.

customer_email_delivery.description: Whether Flint or you send each kind of buyer email. Omitted until you save a value in this section; effective settings fill in Flint's defaults.

fulfillment.description: Fulfillment workflow defaults. Omitted until you save a value in this section; effective settings fill in Flint's defaults.

inventory.description: Inventory defaults, such as the low stock threshold and what happens when stock can't cover a paid order. Omitted until you save a value in this section; effective settings fill in Flint's defaults.

invoices.description: Defaults and policies for the invoices you issue. Omitted until you save a value in this section; effective settings fill in Flint's defaults.

legal.description: Legal links and terms acceptance that checkout shows. Omitted until you save a value in this section; effective settings fill in Flint's defaults.

merchant_id.description: ID of the merchant this resource belongs to.

metadata.description: Stored caller-owned key-value data. See `MetadataInput` for key, value, and size rules.

payment_limits.description: Your own lower and upper limits on payment amounts. Omitted until you save a value in this section; effective settings fill in Flint's defaults.

promotions.description: Whether automatic promotions and promotion codes apply, and how many discounts one order can stack. Omitted until you save a value in this section; effective settings fill in Flint's defaults.

receipts.description: What receipts contain and whether Flint emails them. Omitted until you save a value in this section; effective settings fill in Flint's defaults.

settings_id.description: Unique identifier for this settings, prefixed `set_`.

subscriptions.description: Subscription billing behavior, such as what happens when payment retries run out. Omitted until you save a value in this section; effective settings fill in Flint's defaults.

tax.description: Default tax behavior for new checkouts and orders. Omitted until you save a value in this section; effective settings fill in Flint's defaults.

tax_identity.description: The merchant's legal identity, printed on invoices and credit notes. `null` when none is set.

tipping.description: How tips work at checkout. Omitted until you save a value in this section; effective settings fill in Flint's defaults.

SettlementAmounts.description: Money collected, returned, waived, and still owed on a bill.

outstanding_money.description: Money still owed on the bill, never below zero. Refunds return money already collected and do not add to it.

paid_money.description: Money collected toward the bill, net of reversed payments. Excludes written-off debt.

refunded_money.description: Money returned to the buyer from what was collected toward the bill.

written_off_money.description: Owed money waived as uncollectible. Reduces outstanding_money without increasing paid_money or net_collected_money. Cannot be refunded or used to fund an exchange.

status.description:
Read-only shipment state derived from the shipment's package states. An empty shipment remains a created draft.
- `created`: The shipment leg exists but has not been packed or handed off.
- `packed`: The shipment leg is packed and awaiting carrier handoff.
- `shipped`: The shipment leg was handed to the carrier.
- `in_transit`: The carrier is moving the shipment through its network.
- `out_for_delivery`: The shipment is on its final delivery route.
- `delivered`: The carrier reported successful delivery.
- `delivery_attempted`: The carrier attempted delivery but did not complete it. Follow the carrier instructions before retrying delivery.
- `exception`: A carrier exception is blocking normal progress. Resolve the carrier-reported issue.
- `returned`: The shipment was returned toward or to its origin.
- `voided`: The shipment was voided and will not continue through delivery.

SubscribedLine.description: The subscription offer and billing interval an order line was bought under, with the recurring amount.

recurring_amount_money.description: Line amount for the first renewal, including modifiers and recurring discounts, before shipping and tax. Signup-only discounts are excluded.

SubscribedLineInput.description: Makes an order line a subscription purchase, with the subscription offer and billing interval.

subscription_offer_id.description: Active subscription offer for this catalog variant.

SubscribedLineRequestInput.description: Makes an order line a subscription purchase, with the subscription offer and billing interval.

subscription_offer_id.description: Active subscription offer for this catalog variant.

awaiting_billing_schedule.description: True while an active or trialing subscription on an external billing schedule has no next billing date.

billing_anchor_day.description: UTC day of the month used for monthly and yearly billing. Applies only to Flint-owned schedules.

billing_interval.description: How often the subscription bills now. Read with billing_interval_count: monthly with a count of 3 bills quarterly. A change applies from the next renewal that has not been paid; next_billing_at does not move.

billing_interval_count.description: Number of billing_interval units between charges. Changes with billing_interval.

billing_schedule_owner.description: Who supplies billing dates: flint advances the schedule after each paid renewal; external uses dates you supply. Change it with billing_schedule on PATCH /v1/subscriptions/{subscription_id}.
x-enum-descriptions: Flint computes each next billing date and advances it after every paid renewal.
You set each next billing date. Billing waits until you set `next_billing_at`.

buyer_actions.description: What the buyer can do with the subscription, in this order: cancel, pause, resume, reactivate, update_payment_method, retry_payment, update_delivery, skip, update_billing_interval, update_quantity, swap_items, then renew, under the store's buyer policy. The available cancel and pause actions carry the choices they accept. A buyer's read or change through a customer session on /v1/me, or in Flint's buyer account, lists all twelve every time; a merchant read gets an empty list. update_payment_method is required while a payment is past due, due by next_retry_at when a retry is scheduled, and when the card expires before next_billing_at, due by then.

cancel_at_period_end.description: True when the subscription is scheduled to cancel at scheduled_cancel_at. Schedule with POST /v1/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/cancel; undo with PATCH and cancel_at_period_end false.

cancellation_details.description: Who asked to cancel, when, and why. Present once a cancellation is requested, whether it takes effect at the end of the billing period or right away. Omitted when no one asked, and removed when a scheduled cancellation is undone. See cancellation_reason for voluntary and payment-related cancellations.

cancellation_reason.description: Why the subscription is canceled or scheduled to cancel. Uses cancellation_details.requested_by when recorded, payment_failed for a canceled subscription without a requester, and other for a scheduled cancellation without a requester. Omitted otherwise.
x-enum-descriptions: The buyer asked to cancel.
The merchant asked to cancel.
Payment failed without a recorded cancellation request.
A cancellation is scheduled without a recorded requester.

completed_cycles.description: Billing cycles charged so far, including cycles imported with `billing_start.imported.completed_cycles`. The next renewal order's `subscription_cycle` is this number plus one.

contract_end_at.description: When the recorded contract term ends. Does not move when the subscription pauses or changes plan. Flint does not stop the buyer from canceling earlier.

contract_start_at.description: When the recorded contract term started. Does not move when the subscription pauses or changes plan.

customer.description: Present only when `expand` includes `customer`; `null` when expanded and there is no related customer.

customer_id.description: The customer this subscription bills.

delivery.description: Saved delivery preference with the current delivery method display. Write responses use the same display as GET: fixed shipping reflects the current method configuration, and quoted shipping shows the last paid shipping amount when available.

delivery_hold.description: Current delivery issue that blocks collection. Mutually exclusive with upcoming_delivery_hold.

early_termination_fee_money.description: The fee in the recorded contract terms. Present whenever those terms include a fee. It applies only to a cancellation before contract_end_at. Flint never charges it. Later plan changes do not change this fee.

external_reference_id.description: Caller-owned identifier for this resource in an external system.

inventory_wait.description: Renewal waiting for stock. Included only in merchant responses and omitted from buyer responses.

last_payment_error.description: Latest renewal payment failure, present only while status is past_due and the latest payment failed. Buyer responses omit merchant remediation and sensitive decline signals.

line_items.description: What each renewal bills. Plan edits do not change it. Adding, changing or swapping a line takes that variant's current catalog price, which then stays until the line changes again.

merchant_id.description: ID of the merchant this resource belongs to.

metadata.description: Stored caller-owned key-value data. See `MetadataInput` for key, value, and size rules.

missed_billing_at.description: The billing date whose payment failed, as an RFC3339 timestamp. Present only while status is past_due.

next_billing_at.description: When Flint next starts a scheduled renewal charge, as an RFC3339 timestamp. Present only while a trialing or active subscription has a billing date and isn't set to cancel at the end of its period. Absent when no renewal is scheduled: a paused subscription resumes at scheduled_resume_at, a past_due one reports the failed billing date in missed_billing_at and retries at next_retry_at, an incomplete one retries at next_retry_at, a scheduled start begins at starts_at, one set to cancel ends at scheduled_cancel_at, and an external schedule awaiting a date reports awaiting_billing_schedule.

next_retry_at.description: Recorded automatic payment retry time. Null when no retry time is available.

open_renewal_order_id.description: ID of the paid renewal order whose shipment has not been dispatched. It keeps its committed delivery destination after preference changes and cancellation. Absent when no such renewal order exists. Only renewal orders count; the signup order is not included.

outstanding_money.description: Unpaid balance of the failed renewal order, including tax, shipping and discounts, after payments and credits. Present only while status is past_due and a positive balance remains.

pause_reason.description: Why the subscription is paused: merchant for a pause made with your API key or dashboard, buyer for the buyer's own pause, delivery_action_required for a pause during or after a delivery hold, and payment_failed when renewal payment retries ran out and your dunning settings pause the subscription. Omitted when the subscription is not paused.

payment_method.description: Present only when `expand` includes `payment_method`; `null` when expanded and there is no related payment method.

payment_method_id.description: The saved payment method renewals charge. Change it with PATCH.

promotions.description: Recurring promotions applying to the next charged cycle. Empty when none apply; signup-only and exhausted promotions are excluded.

quantity.description: How many of each line the subscription bills each period, as a whole number; fractional quantities are not supported. A change applies from the next renewal that has not been paid.

recurring_subtotal_money.description: What one billing period's items cost before discounts, shipping, and tax: each line's price with modifiers, times quantity. It changes when items, quantity, or the plan change; editing the plan doesn't change it. For the next charge, use a subscription preview in next_renewal mode.

resume_requested_at.description: When Flint accepted a pending resume request. Set only while paused with a resume Flint has not applied yet. Clears when Flint resumes the subscription or refuses the request.

scheduled_cancel_at.description: When the scheduled cancellation takes effect: trial_end_at while trialing, current_period_end_at while active, or next_retry_at while past_due. Null when cancel_at_period_end is false or no cancellation time is available.

scheduled_resume_at.description: When a pause with a length (pause_duration_cycles) resumes on its own: that many billing intervals after paused_at. Null when the subscription is not paused or the pause has no length, such as a pause until you resume it or the pause Flint starts when a delivery hold runs out.

service_location.description: Omitted for a checkout session credential that doesn't act for the customer the buyer verified.

starts_at.description: When a scheduled start's first billing period begins. Present only until that first payment succeeds.

status.description: Where the subscription is in its lifecycle. Each value says what it means.
x-enum-descriptions: In the free trial. Nothing has been charged.
Current. After a trial it is active while the first charge runs.
Billing is suspended. See pause_reason.
A charge failed and Flint is retrying, or waiting for a new payment method.
Ended. Terminal. This status is final.

TaxConnection.description: The environment's automatic sales tax connection. Before a record exists, identity, version and timestamps are omitted. Read-time business-detail changes and provider pauses do not advance version or send webhooks. Status_reason and supported_actions can also change with the clock as registrations end, without a version change or webhook.

disclosure.description: Current statements the seller must agree to before connecting.

status.description: Whether automatic tax is connected and can calculate tax.
x-enum-descriptions: Automatic tax is not set up. `status_reason` says what is missing; without one, or after a disconnect, you can connect.
Flint is setting up the connection. Read it again until the status changes.
Automatic tax is connected and calculates tax.
Setup stopped or something changed. `status_reason` says what to fix.
Automatic tax is disabled for this connection. You can neither connect nor disconnect it.

status_reason.description: Machine-readable detail for `not_connected` or `attention_required`. `null` when no reason applies. Unknown reasons normalize to `other`.
x-enum-descriptions: Automatic tax is not available for this merchant.
The merchant's verified business details are not complete. Finish onboarding, then connect.
Set a supported `default_line_item_tax_category` in tax settings, then connect.
Add a tax registration that has not ended, then connect.
Automatic tax is temporarily unavailable. Try again later.
Setup did not finish. Connect again to resume it, or disconnect.
A tax registration failed verification. Delete or fix it, then connect again, or disconnect.
The merchant's verified business name or address no longer matches the connected tax account. Writes are refused until Flint reconciles them.
Setup hit a problem that only Flint support can resolve. Writes are refused until it is fixed.
The connection was disconnected. You can connect again.
The connection needs attention for a reason this API does not name.
No reason applies.

supported_actions.description: Lists connect when setup can complete and disconnect when automatic tax can be turned off, based on the connection state for every credential. An empty array means neither action is available. Performing either action requires settings.write.

Call POST /v1/tax-connection/disconnect.

start_date.description: First day the registration applies, inclusive. Flint checks it against each sale's local date. Status and validation use the UTC date. May be up to 365 days in the future.

state.description: US postal state code or DC. Registrations in the same state must have non-overlapping date windows. Uses the US postal abbreviation from ISO 3166-2:US (without the US- prefix).

status.description: Pending until confirmed; then scheduled before start_date, active within the inclusive date window, and ended after end_date. Rejected when verification fails. Removed is returned only by DELETE in its final snapshot.

Confirmed, with a start_date after today (UTC).
Confirmed, and today (UTC) is within its inclusive date window.
Confirmed, with an end_date before today (UTC).
Verification failed.
Returned only by DELETE, in the final snapshot of the deleted registration. This status is final.

created_at.description: When the test clock was created, in real time.

frozen_at.description: The time the test clock shows. Customers created on the clock, and their subscriptions, treat it as the current time. After you advance the clock, `frozen_at` is the time you advanced it to, while `status` is `advancing` and after.

name.description: Your label for the test clock. Omitted when you didn't set one.

status.description: Where the test clock is in its lifecycle. Read it before advancing, and after an advance until it's `ready` or `failed`.
x-enum-descriptions: Stopped at `frozen_at`. You can advance it and create customers on it.

Flint is moving the clock's customers and their subscriptions to `frozen_at`, running the billing that falls due along the way, in order. Resources on the clock can show any time between the previous `frozen_at` and this one until the clock is `ready`. Wait for `test_clock.ready`, or read the clock until its status changes.
Flint couldn't finish an advance. Resources on the clock may have processed only part of it. The clock can't advance again: archive it and create a new one.
Archived with `DELETE`. The clock stays readable but never advances, and no new customer can be created on it. Its customers and subscriptions stay at `frozen_at`. This status is final.

collection.description: How the invoice is collected. Send the invoice's collection object back unchanged, or a new one. merchant_default resolves again from invoice settings when the draft is written.

expected_version.description: Invoice version last read. Required when schedule_entries is present. Required when any of these fields is present: schedule_entries.

external_reference_id.description: Caller-owned identifier for this resource in an external system. Use it as your sync key: it isn't printed on the invoice, and GET /v1/invoices filters on it by exact match. Send null to clear it.

footer.description: Fine print at the bottom of the invoice and PDF. Send null to clear it.

memo.description: Message to the customer, printed on the invoice and PDF. Send null to clear it.

metadata.description: Caller-owned metadata. Omit this field to leave metadata unchanged. Send an object to merge by key, set a key to null to remove it, or set metadata to null to clear all caller-owned metadata. An empty object makes no change. Values can't be empty strings. Keys starting with flint_ are reserved for Flint, are not returned, and cannot be written through the public API.

payment_due.description: When the invoice is due. Send the invoice's payment_due object back unchanged, or a new one. Sending payment_terms captures the term's current revision again.

po_number.description: The buyer's purchase order number, printed on the invoice and PDF. Send null to clear it.

recipient_email.description: Where Flint emails the invoice and its reminders. Required at issue when delivery resolves to email, and when you schedule the issue. Send null to clear it.

reference.description: Your reference for the invoice, printed on the invoice and PDF. Put the buyer's purchase order number in po_number instead. Send null to clear it.

reminders_paused.description: Pauses (true) or resumes (false) the automatic reminder cadence. Accepted only on an open or partially paid invoice with a balance remaining, and only alone or with expected_version: every other field is draft-only. While paused, manual send-reminder calls still work, and invoice.overdue and invoice.late_fee_due still fire. On resume, reminder times that passed while paused do not fire. Sending the current value succeeds without changing the invoice.

remit_to_address.description: Where the buyer sends offline payments, printed on the invoice. Omit it to use the invoice settings remit-to address.

schedule_entries.description: Complete draft payment schedule with at most 14 entries. Validation errors identify the entry by index, such as schedule_entries[3].kind. Enum values are case-sensitive and must not contain surrounding whitespace. Omission preserves the current or default schedule; [] clears the authored schedule. Null is not accepted. On PATCH, include invoice_schedule_entry_id to retain an entry and expected_version to detect concurrent edits.

scheduled_issue_at.description: When Flint issues and delivers this draft, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in the future. A scheduled issue delivers by email, so the draft needs recipient_email. Clearing it cancels the scheduled issue. Send null to clear it.

service_date.description: The calendar date of the billed service, in YYYY-MM-DD format. The invoice and PDF print it as written, without timezone conversion. Send null to clear it.

UpdateLineItemRequest.description: The request body for: Update line item.

description.description: Send null to clear description.

expected_version.description: Order version from the last order read, returned in data.version. Required when any of these fields is present: modifiers, gift_card_recipient, gift_card_face_value_money, subscription.

gift_card_face_value_money.description: Selects the face value of an unpaid, unfunded gift card line within its frozen offer's custom_amount_bounds and reprices the order. Fixed-denomination offers accept only their current value. Omission preserves the value; null is not allowed. Requires expected_version from the order. Checkout credentials may send this field alone or together with gift_card_recipient. The amount and every computed order amount must not exceed 99999999 minor units ($999,999.99 USD). Flint rejects an input or calculation above this ceiling with INVALID_REQUEST and detail INVALID_VALUE at the responsible input field. Lower payment option limits can apply.

amount.description: Amount in the currency's smallest unit, such as cents for USD.

gift_card_recipient.description: Replaces the recipient of an unfunded gift card purchase. Omission preserves it; null clears it. Send expected_version from the order. Send null to clear gift_card_recipient. Requires expected_version.

metadata.description: Caller-owned metadata. Omit this field to leave metadata unchanged. Send an object to merge by key, set a key to null to remove it, or set metadata to null to clear all caller-owned metadata. An empty object makes no change. Values can't be empty strings. Keys starting with flint_ are reserved for Flint, are not returned, and cannot be written through the public API. Send null to clear all metadata.

name.description: Name of the line item.

quantity.description: Replacement quantity, from 1 through 9999. The extended line subtotal, including modifiers, must satisfy the order money ceiling.

subscription.description: Selects an active subscription offer and reprices an unpaid line. Null selects a one-time purchase. Omission preserves the selection. Requires expected_version from the order and clears the delivery selection when terms change. Send null to clear subscription. Requires expected_version.

tax.description: Tax settings for the line item.

unit_price_money.description: Price of one unit. The amount and every computed order amount must not exceed 99999999 minor units ($999,999.99 USD). Flint rejects an input or calculation above this ceiling with INVALID_REQUEST and detail INVALID_VALUE at the responsible input field. Lower payment option limits can apply.

Standard Webhooks v1 HMAC-SHA256 signature in `webhook-signature`, using the endpoint's `whsec_` secret.

WebhookStreamDisconnect.description: Sent on the webhook event stream before the server closes it, with the `reason`. After a backpressure disconnect, resume from `resume_cursor`.

resume_cursor.description: Last event sent before a backpressure disconnect. Reconnect using this value as Last-Event-ID or after.

WebhookStreamGap.description: Sent on the webhook event stream when events could not be replayed from the requested cursor, with a `resume_cursor` to continue from.

WebhookStreamReady.description: Sent when a webhook event stream connects, with the current `cursor`.

WebhookStreamWithheld.description: Sent on the webhook event stream in place of an event that was withheld, such as when the caller lacks a required scope, with the `reason`.

x-enum-descriptions: The merchant's available or pending balance changed.
A new balance transaction (charge, refund, dispute, payout, fee, merchant billing collection, or adjustment) was recorded.
A balance transaction changed state.
A bundle was archived.
A bundle was created.

A bundle's own fields, images, categories, modifier set or components changed. Copied category names and handles, component variant summaries and delivery readiness send no bundle events. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A category was created.
A category was deleted. It can no longer be retrieved.
A category was updated. Assigned product and bundle counts and targeting_reference_count send no category events. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A checkout session was closed before payment completed.
A checkout session was created.
A checkout session expired.

A checkout session was invalidated because its order closed or was paid elsewhere, an invoice, return-resolution, or subscription-plan change ended it, or a replacement session superseded it. Other order edits keep hosted and embedded sessions open and do not send this event.
A checkout session became paid.
A checkout session became partially paid.
A draft credit note was created.
A credit note was issued.
A draft credit note was updated.
A credit note was voided.
A credit note amount was allocated to its invoice.
A credit note allocation was reversed.
A custom domain was archived.
A custom domain changed status.
A customer record was created.
A customer's personal data was erased and its status is now deleted.
A customer record was updated.
A customer deletion request completed and the customer was anonymized.
A buyer requested deletion of their customer account data.
A customer deletion request failed and can be retried.
A customer deletion request entered processing.
A customer deletion request was rejected.
A customer's email preferences changed, because the buyer changed them or the customer's email address changed.
A delivery location set was activated.
A delivery location set was archived.
A delivery location set was created.
A delivery location set was deactivated.
A delivery location set configuration changed.
A delivery method was activated.
A delivery method was archived.
A delivery method was created.
A delivery method was deactivated.
A delivery method configuration changed.
A delivery profile was activated.
A delivery profile was archived.
A delivery profile was created.
A delivery profile was deactivated.
A delivery profile configuration changed.
A delivery rate callback was activated.
A delivery rate callback was archived.
A delivery rate callback was created.
A delivery rate callback was deactivated.
A delivery rate callback configuration changed.
An emergency delivery dependency revocation was created with a safe estimated impact.
A delivery selection became the order's committed fulfillment economics.
A delivery zone was activated.
A delivery zone was archived.
A delivery zone was created.
A delivery zone was deactivated.
A delivery zone expression changed.
First observation of a dispute, in any status.
The inquiry closed without becoming a chargeback.
The dispute status first became lost.
The status entered needs_response or inquiry_needs_response and a response is allowed. This includes inquiry escalation.
The dispute status first became prevented.
Another change to the public dispute representation, including a move to other. Sent only when no condition event applies.
The dispute status first became won.
A merchant environment was granted to a partner app install.
A merchant environment grant was revoked from a partner app install.
An early fraud warning was reported for a payment.
An early fraud warning changed actionability or dispute linkage.
A fulfillment was canceled.
A fulfillment completed: every quantity it covers was fulfilled or canceled.
A fulfillment was created, by checkout or by your call.
A fulfillment failed.
A fulfillment's status or details changed, such as its recipient, schedule, or metadata. Terminal status changes send their own events.
A fulfillment event was recorded from a carrier, pickup flow, appointment system, or other fulfillment source.
A gift card was issued. The masked resource includes its posted, reserved and available value.
A gift card balance, reservation, lifecycle, credential or descriptive association changed.
A gift card funding lot was recorded with face value and consideration provenance.
A gift card funding lot's remaining value or risk restriction changed.
A gift card recipient notification was created. The snapshot includes its recipient, status and version.
A gift card recipient notification's delivery status changed. Retrieve the notification for current delivery history.
An exact gift card redemption was reserved or captured.
A gift card redemption was captured, released, expired or refunded.
An immutable gift card financial movement was posted. Corrections create new transactions.
An inventory count was applied and its variances were committed to inventory.
An inventory level has more protected claims than sellable physical stock.
An inventory level version advanced.
Returned units were received into Inventory, from a Return disposition or against the reservation line that consumed them.
An inventory claim requires a safe merchant action before commerce can continue.
A held or committed inventory claim became insufficiently protected.
An inventory reservation has no active held or committed quantity.
Held inventory quantity became committed order inventory.
Fulfillment consumed committed physical inventory.
An inventory reservation was created with exact location assignments.
A merchant-owned inventory hold reached its deadline.
Held or committed inventory quantity was released.
An inventory transfer reached a terminal state.
Inventory departed a transfer's origin.
Inventory in transit was recorded as lost.
Inventory was received at a transfer's destination.
Inventory in transit was returned to its origin.
Stock returned for a blocked subscription renewal invoice. Flint voids the invoice and charges the renewal on its order.
Collection on a subscription renewal invoice is blocked because the renewal could not get stock.
An invoice was created.
An invoice balance closed with positive applied credit and no positive net collection.
A scheduled invoice could not be issued and remains a draft.
An invoice was issued and became open for collection.
A late fee was added to an invoice balance.
An invoice reached a configured late fee date.
The unpaid remainder of an invoice late fee was waived.
An invoice's outstanding balance was written off as uncollectible.
An invoice passed its payment due date with an outstanding balance.
An invoice balance closed with positive net collection. Collection, allocated credit, waived fees, or reversal recovery can clear the balance.
An invoice became partially paid or received another collection while a balance remained. Sent for online, gift card, and manual payments.
Part of an invoice's payment was refunded.
An invoice's payment was fully refunded.
An invoice reminder is ready to send.
An invoice balance reopened after a payment or credit allocation was reversed. The invoice is open or partially paid.
An invoice was sent to the customer.
An invoice draft, schedule, reminder settings, refund state, or other non-status detail was updated.
An invoice was voided and can no longer be paid.
An invoice email delivery attempt failed.
An invoice email was sent.
An invoice email delivery attempt was suppressed.
A manual (offline) payment was recorded against an invoice.
A manual payment was reversed and its amount returned to the invoice balance.
An invoice payment attempt was canceled.
An invoice payment attempt expired.
An invoice payment attempt failed.
An invoice payment attempt entered processing.
An invoice payment attempt settled successfully. The payment may cover all or part of the invoice balance.

A merchant's payment, payout, or onboarding readiness was observed in live or sandbox mode after an account or verification update, account reconciliation, a payout capability change, or a processing pause or resumption. Account reconciliation includes payment capability activation or loss. A payment capability change alone may not send this event; read GET /v1/merchant to check readiness.
The merchant profile, status, API version, logo, or icon changed.
The amount the merchant owes Flint or owns as account credit changed.
Flint issued a merchant billing invoice.
A merchant billing invoice changed status.
A modifier group was archived.
A modifier group was created.
A modifier group's own fields or modifiers changed. Owned collections are included in this object. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A modifier set was archived.
A modifier set was created.
A modifier set's own fields, groups or inline modifiers changed. Owned collections are included in this object. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
An open order closed. closed_reason says why: paid, closed_by_merchant, checkout_expired, written_off, superseded, or return_resolution_canceled.
An order was created.
An order has an inventory failure that requires operator action.
An order inventory exception was resolved.
An order became fully paid, including by a manual payment on its invoice. Use payment_intent.succeeded for each successful online payment.
An order first became partially paid, including by a manual payment on its invoice. Use payment_intent.succeeded for each successful online payment.
An order became partially refunded.
An order became fully refunded.
An order was updated.
A shipment package was created.
A shipment package changed, including status, details, or contents. List the package items to read its contents.
A partner app install was created.
An environment grant's permissions changed: the merchant re-authorized, or you removed or narrowed a permission.
The install was revoked by the merchant or by you. revoked_by says which.
A partner app install changed.
A payment intent was canceled.
A payment intent was created.
A payment intent authorization expired before capture.
A payment intent fulfillment hold was activated or released.
A payment attempt failed.
A payment was submitted and is awaiting its final outcome.
The payment requires a customer action such as 3D Secure authentication.
The payment was authorized and is awaiting capture.
A payment intent succeeded.
A payment intent changed without entering a more specific lifecycle status.
A payment link was created.
A payment link changed, including being activated or deactivated. Sales through the link don't send this event.
A payment method became active and can be charged.
A saved payment method was deleted. It stays readable and can't be charged again.
Saving a payment method failed.
A payment review was resolved or closed by a payment lifecycle change.
A payment was placed into manual review.
A declined review's refund failed, so the review is open again and needs a decision.
A payout to the merchant's bank was canceled.
A payout to the merchant's bank was created.
A payout failed and funds were returned to the balance.
A completed payout was reversed.
A payout arrived at the merchant's bank.
A payout changed state.
A payout destination was removed. It stays readable by ID with status archived.
A payout destination (bank account) was added.
A payout destination was disabled.
A payout destination was updated.
The merchant's payout schedule or settings changed.
A product was archived. Its variants were archived with it and send no events of their own.
A product was created. Each variant it created sends product_variant.created.

A product's own fields, options, images, categories or modifier set changed. Variant changes send product_variant events instead, although they also change the product's rollups and version. Rollups (default_variant, price_range, active_variant_count, variant_count, available_for_sale and delivery_configuration_status) and copied category names and handles send no product events. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A variant was archived on its own. Archiving its product sends only product.archived.
A product variant was created.

A product variant was updated. Copied selected option names and values, available_for_sale, effective_images and delivery readiness send no variant events. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A promotion was archived. Its codes were archived with it and send no events of their own.
A promotion was created. Each code it created sends promotion_code.created.

A promotion was updated. Changes to codes_summary, uses_count, available and unavailable_reason, including redemptions and schedule boundaries, send no promotion events. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A promotion code was archived on its own. Archiving its promotion sends only promotion.archived.
A promotion code was created.

A promotion code was updated. Changes to uses_count, available and unavailable_reason, including redemptions and schedule boundaries, send no promotion code events. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A refund was created.
A refund failed.
A refund partially succeeded.
A refund succeeded in full.
A refund changed without entering a more specific lifecycle status.
An asynchronous report reached a terminal generation failure.
An asynchronous report completed and its authenticated CSV download is ready.
A Return was canceled.
A Return completed after every required merchandise and buyer-value obligation cleared.
A Return was created.
The merchant or policy automation recorded line-level Return decisions.
A completed Return was reopened for additional work.
A Return or one of its line-level progress projections changed.
A merchandise disposition was recorded for a Return.
A Return disposition changed execution state.
Acceptance was decided for a Return inspection observation.
A Return inspection observation was recorded.
A Return inspection observation was superseded by an auditable correction.
A Return receipt observation was recorded.
A Return receipt observation was superseded by an auditable correction.
An unmatched Return receipt line was verified against the expected merchandise.
A proposed buyer-value resolution was created for a Return.
A Return resolution changed proposal, gate, effect, or fulfillment state.
A shipment was created.
A shipment changed, including status, details, or package count.
A subscription's first paid period was collected, or it was created already paid or imported, so it is active. Sent once per subscription.
A subscription was canceled.
A subscription was set to cancel at the end of its billing period or trial, or in place of its next payment retry. `scheduled_cancel_at` says when.
A subscription was created.
A subscription billing cycle was skipped without a charge.
A subscription renewal needs an address, method, or rate correction before it can be charged.
A subscription delivery hold is approaching its pause date.
A subscription's delivery preference changed. Paid, unshipped renewals keep their existing destination.
A subscription used its automatic payment retry budget.
A subscription renewal failed and is past due.
A subscription was paused.
A subscription billing attempt succeeded.
A subscription moved to another plan, or to its plan's current lines and prices. When the change bills a new period, subscription.payment_succeeded is sent with it.
A subscription's scheduled cancellation was undone, so it renews as usual.
A subscription renewal is approaching.
A paused subscription was resumed.
A subscription trial is approaching its end.
A subscription changed and no more specific subscription event describes the change.
A subscription delivery method migration finished. Its counts and failures identify which subscriptions moved.
A subscription payment retry was created.
A subscription payment retry failed.
A subscription payment retry succeeded.

The automatic tax connection's public state changed, including setup, support disable, or a registration change. Read-time business-detail changes and provider pauses send no event; read the connection again when automatic tax fails.
A sandbox test clock started advancing to its new frozen_at.
A sandbox test clock was archived.
A sandbox test clock was created.
A sandbox test clock couldn't finish advancing. Resources on the clock may have processed only part of the advance. Flint records test_clock.failed after every event the advance caused.

A sandbox test clock finished advancing. Flint records test_clock.ready after every event the advance caused. Deliveries can still arrive in any order; GET /v1/webhook-events lists them all once the clock is ready.

BearerAuth.bearerFormat: Flint API key, partner install token, or short-lived Flint session token
BearerAuth.description: Flint secret API key, CLI OAuth access token, installation-scoped partner token, or session token sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Route-specific partner access and scopes are declared by x-flint-partner-access and x-flint-partner-required-scopes. Secret API keys use the flint_live_ or flint_test_ prefix; keep ordinary secret keys server-side. The first-party docs playground uses a dedicated sandbox-only sample key exception.

CheckoutSessionBearer.description: The checkout credential from checkout_auth_token, sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>. It acts for one checkout session and its order. Accepted only by the operations that list it.

CustomerSessionBearer.description: The customer session secret (`flint_cses_...`), sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. Accepted only by `/v1/me`. Keep it on your server: Flint has no browser credential, and your backend relays the buyer's account calls.

InvoiceAccessTokenBearer.description: Invoice access token from the invoice's public URL. Accepted only for that invoice's buyer detail, PDF, and checkout-session endpoints.

OnboardingSessionBearer.description: Short-lived onboarding token returned by POST /v1/onboarding/verify-email. The credential selects the environment; the onboarding session token acts in the merchant's default sandbox. Refresh stays bound to the launch token's sandbox. Live onboarding requires a live API key or live CLI login.

info.description: Flint's public /v1 API for payments, checkout, invoices, subscriptions, catalog, customers, returns, inventory, money movement, webhooks, and developer operations. Live keys and sandbox-bound test keys use the same API hostname; the key selects live or sandbox data. Keep ordinary secret API keys server-side. The first-party docs playground uses a dedicated sandbox-only sample key exception. A request body can be up to 1 MiB unless an operation documents a lower limit; a larger body returns 413 with the REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LARGE error code.
