get.description: Returns a paginated ledger of balance-affecting transactions, including availability timing and related public resources. Default order: occurred_at descending, then balance_transaction_id descending.

parameters.description: Optional 3-letter currency filter.
parameters.name: currency

parameters.description: Lists the balance transactions this payout carried, newest first. Their `net_money` sums to the payout's `amount_money`. Works in any payout status once the payout's contents are prepared, usually minutes after it is created. Returns `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` with `Retry-After` while they are prepared, and `409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` with `reason: not_itemized` for a payout that doesn't list its contents, such as a manual payout.
parameters.name: payout_id

parameters.description: Exact-match filter on `order_id`.
parameters.name: order_id

parameters.description: Include related objects in the response. Supported expansions: order. Each expansion resolves with one batched lookup per page. Expansion requires money_movement.balance_transactions.read plus commerce.orders.read. Limits: at most 10 unique expand paths per request.
parameters.name: expand

x-enum-descriptions: Include the full order object in `order`.

parameters.description: Optional balance transaction type filter. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: type

x-enum-descriptions: A payment reached your balance. Positive, and `fee_money` is its processing fee plus any add-on fees.
A refund took money out of your balance. Negative, with a `fee_money` of 0: the original payment's processing fee isn't returned.
A dispute took the disputed amount, and any processor dispute fee, out of your balance. Card chargebacks and ACH bank returns both post this type.
The disputed amount came back to your balance. `fee_money` is negative only when the processor also returned its dispute fee on this row.
A payment that had already posted to your balance failed afterward, such as an ACH debit the buyer's bank rejected.
A refund failed, and its amount came back to your balance.
Money left your balance for your bank. Negative. Each payout has exactly one.
A payout failed, and its amount returned to your balance.
A canceled payout's amount returned to your balance.
A paid payout was pulled back from your bank, and its amount returned to your balance.
An advance your processor recorded on your account. Most accounts never see this type.
Settled funds that repay an advance.
Funds moved from your balance into a reserve. It changes what you can pay out, not what you earned.
Reserved funds returned to your balance.
A correction posted against your balance. `description` says what it covers.
Flint collected what you owe Flint out of your balance.
A collection came back to your balance.

parameters.description: Filter by related_resource.resource_type. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: related_resource_type

x-enum-descriptions: The movement was caused by a payment intent, such as a payment or a payment that failed after it posted.
The movement was caused by a refund, such as the refund or a failed refund coming back.
The movement was caused by a dispute or its reversal.
The movement was caused by a payout, such as the payout itself or one that failed, was canceled, or was reversed.
The movement is tied to a payout destination.
The movement is tied to a Flint billing invoice, such as a collection from your balance.

parameters.description: Filter by related_resource.resource_id.
parameters.name: related_resource_id

parameters.description: Optional balance transaction status filter. Without it, the list returns transactions in every status. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: status

x-enum-descriptions: The funds are on your balance but can't be paid out yet. `available_at` is when Flint expects them to become available.
The funds can be paid out.

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on occurred_at.

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on occurred_at.
parameters.name: occurred_before

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on available_at.
parameters.name: available_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on available_at.
parameters.name: available_before

parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20.
parameters.name: page_size

parameters.description: Opaque next_page_token from the previous response. Omit on the first request. You may change `page_size` between pages. Reuse it with the same endpoint, filters, sort, and request context. Do not parse or construct tokens. An invalid, expired, or mismatched token returns a validation error.

parameters.description: Filter by the status each session has when read. A session past expires_at lists as expired even before its stored status is updated, unless payment work keeps it open, in which case it lists as open. A page can hold fewer sessions than page_size. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: status

An operation already underway determines the resource's next available action (reason `in_progress`). Payment details cannot be saved during a return checkout (reason `return_checkout`). The resource's current state does not support this action (reason `unsupported_state`). A resource already occupies the requested key or slot (`ALREADY_EXISTS`). A request with the same idempotency key is still in progress (`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_PROGRESS`). The idempotency key was reused with a different request body (`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`). A count prevents another request of this kind (`LIMIT_REACHED`). Flint is finishing other work on the resource (`OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS`). The requested payment option is not available for this merchant, amount, or checkout. The amount_out_of_range reason means the amount is outside this payment option's limits (`PAYMENT_OPTION_UNAVAILABLE`). References to this resource prevent the change (`RESOURCE_IN_USE`). The resource changed and the request must be rebuilt from its current state (`VERSION_CONFLICT`).

patch.description: Updates the mutable fields of a checkout session. A merchant credential can update metadata and external_reference_id, including after the session ends. Send external_reference_id as null to clear it, or metadata as null to clear all metadata. On a session with a subscription_plan_id, either credential can send subscription_terms with the buyer's billing interval and quantity while the session is open and no payment is in progress; a change reprices the signup order and releases the delivery selection. The session's own checkout credential can also send buyer_contact and timezone while the session is open. The buyer_contact field saves the email and phone the buyer entered; send a contact field as null to clear it. The timezone field records the buyer's IANA time zone, which Flint uses for times in the emails it sends the buyer. Saving the same values again changes nothing.

post.description: Checks the code the buyer typed. A right code makes the checkout act for the customer with that email, and creates the customer, with a customer.created event, when none exists. The checkout can then save the buyer's card with save_payment_method on POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/pay, and list and pay with that customer's saved cards. The order's customer does not change until the payment succeeds. Only the checkout_auth_token in the response acts for that customer. Send it as the Bearer credential from then on. Every other credential for the session, including earlier checkout_auth_token values and hosted checkout links, keeps working for the checkout and acts for no customer, so it lists no saved cards and pays with none. A buyer who opens the link on another device confirms an email there to use them, and from then on only that device's new credential acts for a customer. If the response is lost after the code was accepted, the credential you sent still works. Send the same code again with it while the code is valid, which counts as another try and returns a new credential for the same customer, or request a new code. A wrong, expired, or replaced code fails with `INVALID_REQUEST` and an `INVALID_VALUE` detail on `code`, and so does a used code once the checkout was confirmed again, any code after its 5th try, any code for an email past its limit on wrong tries, or a code whose email's customer changed its email or was deleted after the code was sent. If the checkout stops offering saved payment details before the code is confirmed, such as when the merchant turns them off, the request fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `not_offered`. A credential that already acts for a customer fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `already_applied`, and confirming never replaces a customer the merchant named. Once the customer whose email the buyer confirmed changes that email or is deleted, the checkout acts for no customer, and the buyer can confirm the customer's new email or another one. A checkout opened from a checkout reminder link acts for no customer the buyer confirmed earlier, so its buyer confirms an email again. A texted code for saved details binds the checkout the same way, but the new credential opens only the cards saved with that number: it lists and pays with no card saved by email, and reads no customer details. A texted code checks once, so after a lost answer request a new code. A code for purpose confirm_saved_payment_method keeps the session's credential, so the response omits checkout_auth_token and carries payment_method_save on the checkout session. A texted code saves the card with the number when the number already opens the customer's saved details or the customer has none yet; otherwise payment_method_save.email_confirmation_required turns true, and an emailed code finishes the save. An emailed code alone saves the card by email. After success, a retry with the same idempotency key and code returns the stored answer and credential to any credential of the session. After failure, a retry checks the code again and counts as another try.

post.description: Issues a draft credit note and freezes its number, lines, and totals. Provide allocation to issue and apply credit to its invoice atomically, or refund to initiate a linked refund on a paid invoice. Allocation and refund cannot be combined. Omit allocation.amount_money to apply the smaller of the credit available after issue and the invoice's outstanding balance. An explicit amount must be positive, use the invoice's currency, and fit both balances. The result includes credit_note_allocation when allocation is requested. Idempotency-Key is required and is retained for as long as the issue's effects exist, scoped to merchant, environment, credit note, and key. Reuse the key with the identical request to recover the original credit note and allocation. Recover an allocation after a lost response by listing this note's allocations with idempotency_key=issue:<issue key>. For refunds, list this note's refunds filtered by the original idempotency_key. A pending refund is accepted but has not completed. Without allocation or refund, issuance leaves the invoice balance unchanged. Issue validates the stored preview against current shared creditable pools. A fitting correction whose preview changed fails with `VERSION_CONFLICT`, which includes the credit note and `current_version`: replace its existing corrections with PATCH using the current expected_version, review the recalculated amounts, and issue again. A stored correction exceeding the remaining pool fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `not_offered`. Update the draft lines before issuing again. Affected historical tax allocations fail with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `credit_note_tax_reconciliation_required`.

post.description: Rotates a customer session secret and refresh token without a merchant API key. Reusing a rotated refresh token revokes the session family. Use one fixed idempotency key per session: Flint scopes the key to the refresh token, so concurrent refreshes replay the same pair. On `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_PROGRESS`, retry with the same key and token.

parameters.description: Required. A retry with the same key and refresh token within 24 hours replays the rotated secret and refresh token. After that, the old refresh token counts as reused: Flint revokes the session and returns 401 INVALID_CREDENTIAL with reason revoked.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of customers for the authenticated merchant. Without a status filter, returns active and deletion_processing customers; deleted customers appear only when the filter names deleted. Default order: created_at descending, then customer_id descending.

parameters.description: Filter by status. Omitted, the list leaves out deleted rows; name deleted to include them. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: status

x-enum-descriptions: The customer can be changed and used for new purchases.
Deletion was approved and is in progress. The customer can't be changed, charged, or signed in to.
The customer's personal data was erased. Only its ID, created_at, and the records that reference it remain. It can't be changed or restored. This status is final.

parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20.
parameters.name: page_size

parameters.description: Opaque next_page_token from the previous response. Omit on the first request. You may change `page_size` between pages. Reuse it with the same endpoint, filters, sort, and request context. Do not parse or construct tokens. An invalid, expired, or mismatched token returns a validation error.
parameters.name: page_token

parameters.description: Search across customer_id, name, email, phone number, and external_reference_id. Text fields match any part of the value, and %, _ and \ are ordinary characters, not wildcards. IDs match from the start and need the type prefix, such as cus_01.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Exact-match filter on the caller-owned external reference ID.
parameters.name: external_reference_id

parameters.description: Exact whole-address match after trimming surrounding whitespace. Case is ignored and accents are kept: `Ana@example.com` matches `ana@example.com`, but `josé@example.com` doesn't match `jose@example.com`.
parameters.name: email

parameters.description: Byte-sensitive whole-value match on the opaque customer segment. Whitespace, casing, Unicode, and commas are literal.
parameters.name: segment

parameters.description: Filter by merchant verification, independently of email verification.
parameters.name: is_merchant_verified

parameters.description: Exact match on a full E.164 phone number, such as `+14155551234`. The leading plus is required.
parameters.name: phone

parameters.description: Sandbox only. Exact-match filter on `test_clock_id`. A live credential gets `403 FORBIDDEN` with reason `test_mode_required`.

parameters.description: Field to sort by. Defaults to created_at; ties are broken by customer_id.
parameters.name: sort_by

x-enum-descriptions: Display name of the resource.

patch.description: Applies a sparse update to a customer. Changing email requires customer_account.mode to be merchant_hosted; otherwise the update fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `managed_externally`. To change the email of a customer who signs in to your Flint-hosted account, create a customer session for the customer and send POST /v1/me/email-change-requests with the new email; the customer confirms it with the codes Flint emails them. If Flint cannot read the account settings, the update fails with a retryable `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and the customer is unchanged.

post.description: Signs the buyer in to your Flint-hosted customer account as this customer. Works for 15 minutes and one open. The url is a bearer credential. Flint returns it only in this response and in a retry with the same idempotency key, so send it only to the buyer and keep it out of logs. A call with a new key creates another link; earlier links keep working until they expire. Send no request body or an empty object ({}). Requires customers.sessions.write. Idempotency is scoped to the merchant, credential, environment, and this customer's route. A replay returns the original link without extending its lifetime or replenishing its open. Without an idempotency key, each call creates a new link and has no replay result. If Flint cannot retain a result after minting, contact support with the request ID before sending a new request.

parameters.description: Flint customer ID.
parameters.name: customer_id

parameters.description: Optional. A retry with the same key and request within 24 hours returns the original result instead of repeating it.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

parameters.description: Your own ID for this request, such as a log or trace ID, 1 to 128 visible ASCII characters. Flint stores it as client_request_id on the request log. The X-Request-Id response header is Flint's request ID, not this value.
parameters.name: X-Request-Id

409.description: The verification is pending, used, or expired, the customer email changed, or the customer is being deleted. The resource's current state does not allow this action (`ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`). The resource already reflects the action's outcome (reason `already_applied`). An operation already underway determines the resource's next available action (reason `in_progress`). The resource has not reached the status required for this action (reason `status_not_reached`). The resource's final status prevents this action (reason `terminal_status`). A request with the same idempotency key is still in progress (`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_PROGRESS`). The idempotency key was reused with a different request body (`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`).

post.description: Delivery callback endpoints pin shared outbound callback transport configuration. Creation publishes immutable revision 1. signing_methods defaults to ["jwt"]. JWTs use Flint's public JWKS and this callback's delivery_rate_callback_id as aud. Verify body_sha256 against the exact request bytes. The jwt method sends Authorization: Bearer, and the hmac method sends webhook-signature and Flint-Signing-Key-Ids. Every request includes webhook-id and webhook-timestamp. A shared secret and key_id are issued and returned once only when hmac is included. It starts inactive.

post.description: Sandbox only. Simulates the card network's ruling on a dispute that needs a response. Flint submits Stripe's test evidence for the `outcome`, and the ruling arrives through the dispute's usual webhook events, as a real one would. Send `won` or `lost` for a chargeback in `needs_response`, and `inquiry_closed` or `escalated` for an inquiry in `inquiry_needs_response`. The response is the dispute after the evidence is submitted, usually `under_review` or `inquiry_under_review`. Stripe decides shortly after, with no fixed timing. Requires `payments.disputes.write`. If you don't receive a response, retry with the same idempotency key, or read the dispute.

post.description: Completing a merchant_logo or merchant_icon file requires a live-mode credential or a Dashboard session in any selected environment. Test credentials fail with `FORBIDDEN` and reason `live_mode_required`. After PUT succeeds, complete the file to process its image. Returns the ready file; completing a ready file again returns it. Send no request body or {}. Completing before the bytes arrive returns ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason status_not_reached and current_status awaiting_upload. Attach the returned file_id as images[].file_id before expires_at, 24 hours after processing. Completion requires the purpose's write scope, with the same merchant-wide branding and environment boundaries as createFile. Partner installs can upload commerce images but cannot upload merchant_logo or merchant_icon: live install credentials receive INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE with scope_requirement because merchants.profile.write is not grantable to installs. Idempotency is scoped to merchant, credential, environment, route, and file_id. A replay returns the original result; it does not extend upload or attachment deadlines. After a lost completion response, repeat this route with the same key and file_id.

Reuse it with the same endpoint, filters, sort, and request context. Do not parse or construct tokens. An invalid, expired, or mismatched token returns a validation error.

parameters.name: event_type

x-enum-descriptions: A scan reported by a carrier.
Recorded when the status of the fulfillment, a shipment, or a package changes. `previous_status` and `current_status` give the transition, and `subject_type` says which resource changed.
Recorded when a package is handed to the carrier. Status transitions are normally reported as `status_changed`; read `current_status` for the new status.
Recorded when the carrier starts moving a package through its network. Status transitions are normally reported as `status_changed`; read `current_status` for the new status.
Recorded when a package goes out on its final delivery route. Status transitions are normally reported as `status_changed`; read `current_status` for the new status.
Recorded when the carrier reports delivery. Status transitions are normally reported as `status_changed`; read `current_status` for the new status.
Recorded when the carrier attempts delivery without completing it. Status transitions are normally reported as `status_changed`; read `current_status` for the new status.
Recorded when a package's tracking details change. `custom_details` lists the changed details.
Recorded when a carrier exception blocks a package's progress. Status transitions are normally reported as `status_changed`; read `current_status` for the new status.
Recorded when a package is returned toward its origin. Status transitions are normally reported as `status_changed`; read `current_status` for the new status.
An event you define with `message` and `custom_details`.

The merchant recorded cash paid to the buyer outside Flint, taken off the balance. Negative.

A failed refund of the card's purchase restored its value. Positive.
A failed purchase refund's value moved to replacement cards. This entry moves 0 on the original card, and each replacement card posts a `purchase_refund_recovery`.

To recover the command's effects after a lost response, list inventory adjustments with the same idempotency_key, or list inventory movements with that idempotency_key.

patch.description: Replace a count's complete observation set atomically. expected_version is required when replacing observations. Send every item exactly once with the count's current expected_version and each observation's required expected_physical_version. Read the level before physically counting; zero is valid for a missing level. Every assertion must match locked current stock or the whole save is refused. Preserve saved quantities and fences for unchanged lines. Recount affected items before supplying fresh fences, even when quantities are unchanged. Omitted condition quantities retain the matching level snapshot's values. occurred_at records provenance and does not reconstruct historical stock. Idempotency is scoped to the authenticated merchant, environment, and endpoint. Its fingerprint includes the canonical request body. To recover the command's effects after a lost response, read the inventory count by ID.

post.description: Set action to apply or cancel an open physical count. The apply action sets inventory levels to the counted quantities and needs an observation on every line. The cancel action closes the count without changing stock. VERSION_CONFLICT on apply also covers a stale saved physical observation with no corresponding field in this request; these details omit param. Recount affected items and save the complete observations before applying again. Physical changes after observation require recounts, including at a trading location; holds and commitments alone do not invalidate observations. Stock-moving transitions return a result with inventory_count as its primary resource and inventory_levels for the levels changed. Idempotency is scoped to the authenticated merchant, environment, and endpoint. Its fingerprint includes the canonical request body. To recover the command's effects after a lost response, read the inventory count by ID.

Filter by inventory_item_status to see only the levels behind items that can be sold. Levels are strongly consistent individually, but pages may reflect different committed instants. parameters.description: Filter by inventory item.
parameters.name: inventory_item_id

parameters.description: Filter by Location.
parameters.name: location_id

parameters.description: Filter by the status of the inventory item the level belongs to. Only active items can be routed or reserved. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: inventory_item_status

x-enum-descriptions: Available for use.
Unavailable for use; can be made available again.

parameters.description: True selects levels with available quantity; false selects levels with zero available quantity. Omit for all levels.

parameters.description: True selects levels with unavailable physical stock; false selects levels with none. Omit for all levels.
parameters.name: has_unavailable_condition

parameters.description: True selects levels with a shortage; false selects levels with none. Omit for all levels.
parameters.name: has_shortage

parameters.description: Search inventory item ID, name, SKU, or barcode. Case-insensitive substring match.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on available_quantity.
parameters.name: min_available_quantity

parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on available_quantity.
parameters.name: max_available_quantity

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on updated_at.
parameters.name: updated_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on updated_at.
parameters.name: updated_before

parameters.description: Include related objects in the response. Supported expansions: inventory_item. The expansion resolves with one batched lookup per page. Expansion requires commerce.inventory.read. Limits: at most 10 unique expand paths per request.

Filter by idempotency_key to recover the movements a command produced. Send sort_direction=desc to read the newest movements first. A request with the same idempotency key is still in progress (`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_PROGRESS`). The idempotency key was reused with a different request body (`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`). Current eligible inventory cannot satisfy the complete demand (`INVENTORY_INSUFFICIENT`). A value is outside the bound the resource's current state allows (`LIMIT_EXCEEDED`). The resource changed and the request must be rebuilt from its current state (`VERSION_CONFLICT`).

x-enum-descriptions: The invoice was created as a draft.
The invoice was issued: its document is frozen and it can be paid.
Flint emailed the invoice. It is recorded together with `delivery_sent`, which names the delivery attempt and recipient.
An email delivery of the invoice was sent. `invoice_delivery_attempt_id` and `to_email` name the attempt and recipient.
A reminder email was sent. `invoice_delivery_attempt_id` and `to_email` name the attempt and recipient.
The customer opened the invoice from its link for the first time.
A payment attempt on the invoice started. `invoice_payment_attempt_id` names it.
A payment was applied to the invoice. `payment_intent_id` and `amount_money` say which payment and how much.
A payment made outside Flint was recorded on the invoice.
A recorded manual payment was reversed.
A refund of a payment on the invoice succeeded. `refund_id` names it.
The invoice was voided, so it can no longer be paid.
The merchant replaced the invoice's public link. The old link stopped working.
Collection on a subscription renewal invoice is blocked because the renewal couldn't get stock. `collection_block_reason` says why.
Stock returned for a blocked subscription renewal invoice, which ends the block. `collection_block_reason` says why.
A draft, schedule, reminder setting, refund state, or other non-status detail of the invoice changed.
The outstanding balance was written off as uncollectible. `written_off_money` is the amount.
A payment on the invoice is still processing. `expected_amount_money` is what it is expected to settle.
A scheduled issue failed, and the invoice remains a draft. `error_code` says why.
The invoice passed its due date with a balance outstanding.
A reminder is ready to send.
The invoice reached a configured late fee date.
A late fee was added to the invoice. `invoice_late_fee_id` names it.
A late fee was waived. `invoice_late_fee_id` names it.
Applied credit closed the invoice's balance with no net payment collected. `credit_money` is the credit applied.

post.description: Returns the current open invoice checkout session and aligned card attempt when they still match the invoice balance and collection run. A newly created session and attempt share the fixed expiration of the active invoice public-link generation. Unexpired sessions are reused regardless of remaining lifetime; active payment work returns a resolving conflict instead of creating competing collection. When the invoice's order has items to deliver, a new session offers the delivery methods in settings.checkout.default_delivery_method_ids, and the request fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `configuration_required` when those methods cannot deliver every item. return_url sets where the checkout sends the buyer after paying. A reused session takes a new return_url only until a payment starts on it, and keeps the one it has after that.

409.description: The resource's current state does not allow this action (`ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`). The named resource needs configuration before this action (reason `configuration_required`). The resource does not offer this action or option (reason `not_offered`). The order already collected payment (reason `payment_collected`). Flint can't confirm the payment state automatically and must reconcile it before more money moves (reason `reconciliation_required`). The resource's final status prevents this action (reason `terminal_status`). The resource's current state does not support this action (reason `unsupported_state`). The delivery quote or selection must be replaced (`DELIVERY_REQUOTE_REQUIRED`). A request with the same idempotency key is still in progress (`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_PROGRESS`). The idempotency key was reused with a different request body (`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`). Current eligible inventory cannot satisfy the complete demand (`INVENTORY_INSUFFICIENT`). A count prevents another request of this kind (`LIMIT_REACHED`). The order reached its lifetime limit of payment intents (reason `payment_intents_per_order`). The merchant must complete a readiness step before this operation (`MERCHANT_NOT_READY`). Flint is finishing other work on the resource (`OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS`). A payment attempt is still active (`PAYMENT_ATTEMPT_ACTIVE`). The requested payment option is not available for this merchant, amount, or checkout. The amount_out_of_range reason means the amount is outside this payment option's limits (`PAYMENT_OPTION_UNAVAILABLE`). The payment amount is outside this option's accepted range (reason `amount_out_of_range`). ACH debit isn't offered because the order's line items don't show whether the purchase is for goods or services (reason `transaction_purpose_unresolved`). References to this resource prevent the change (`RESOURCE_IN_USE`). The resource changed and the request must be rebuilt from its current state (`VERSION_CONFLICT`).

get.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. Returns which of the merchant's optional email categories the customer's current email receives in the selected merchant environment. A category the buyer never changed is on. Email preferences exist only for a customer with an email: without one, the read fails with `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. Receipts and other transactional email always send.

get.description: Returns the current buyer's usable wallet cards in newest-first order. Each flint_wallet_card_id is an opaque per-store handle. store_payment_method_id is null until this store holds a copy. Requires a customer session minted from a live email-code buyer login at a Flint-hosted store account, including a login narrowed to a custom domain. Email links, checkout sessions, grants, merchant-created sessions, and API keys can't see the wallet and get a not-found response. Live and sandbox wallets are isolated. The full card collection is returned in one page. Flint wallet support must be enabled. Default order: most recently added card first.

post.description: Records the buyer's consent to save an independent store copy for off-session payments, including subscriptions. Call only after the buyer agrees. Requires a live email-code buyer login and an enabled Flint wallet at a Flint-hosted store account. Supply a flint_wallet_card_id from listMeFlintWalletCards. Confirm client_setup with Stripe.js confirmSetup, then poll GET /v1/me/payment-methods/{payment_method_id} until active before changing a subscription through PATCH /v1/me/subscriptions/{subscription_id} with payment_method_id. Setup may request authentication. Removing the platform card or revoking store consent blocks the copy immediately. An idempotency key is optional and scoped to the store, customer, card handle, and key. Responses are retained for 24 hours. After a copy is revoked, retries with any key bound to that copy are refused. Get new consent and use a new key to create another copy. Retry a lost response with the same key. Concurrent requests for the same card at this store share one copy and setup. A failed off-session charge can still require the buyer to return through the existing card-update link. Accept an empty body or {}.

Replacing a code invalidates saved access; save again with fresh proof. Saved access does not permit spending or reveal a full code. get.summary: Get one of the current buyer's invoices

post.description: Accepts a customer session, which limits the request to that customer's invoices, or the access token from this invoice's public link, which limits it to this invoice. The request cannot select a customer_id. Returns the current open invoice checkout session and aligned card attempt when they still match the invoice balance and collection run. A newly created session and attempt share the fixed expiration of the active invoice public-link generation. Unexpired sessions are reused regardless of remaining lifetime; active payment work returns a resolving conflict instead of creating competing collection. When the invoice's order has items to deliver, a new session offers the delivery methods in settings.checkout.default_delivery_method_ids, and the request fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `configuration_required` when those methods cannot deliver every item. return_url sets where the checkout sends the buyer after paying. A reused session takes a new return_url only until a payment starts on it, and keeps the one it has after that.

get.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Returns a read-only, human-readable history log for an order. Use it to render timelines and debug what happened, not as a source of truth, ledger, or webhook replacement. Read the owning resource for authoritative state: the order for balances and status, the payment for payment state, the refund for refund outcomes, and the checkout session for checkout state. Do not sum balance_delta_money to compute an order balance. Informational rows such as payment_failed, refund_failed, and checkout_session_expired have a zero balance delta. The default order is newest first. Use sort_direction=asc for chronological timeline rendering. A typical chronological log might show created, payment_failed, payment, refund, then refund_failed; each row gives one reference to click through for the authoritative resource. Default order: created_at descending, then order_activity_id descending.

Reuse it with the same endpoint, filters, sort, and request context. Do not parse or construct tokens. An invalid, expired, or mismatched token returns a validation error.

parameters.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc.

get.summary: Get one of the current buyer's Return resolutions

post.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Create or reuse a hosted or embedded checkout session for the buyer's balance on a replacement order linked to this return resolution. The response is `200` when it reuses an existing session and `201` when it creates one. Omit surface to use hosted. The same surface reuses the open session; changing surface replaces an idle session and is refused while a payment is in progress. Use redirects to set where the buyer goes after paying or canceling. The return_url field is an alias for redirects.success_url on hosted checkout or payment_return_url on embedded checkout and must be an address of the merchant's customer account. A reused session takes a new success destination only until a payment starts, then keeps its existing destination.

post.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. Starts one manual collection attempt on a past-due subscription. Send no body, or an empty object. Poll the returned retry for the outcome. While cancellation is scheduled, a new buyer retry fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `cancellation_scheduled`, with `current_status` `past_due`. First use PATCH /v1/me/subscriptions/{subscription_id} with cancel_at_period_end false to keep the subscription; retry_payment becomes available again if the other retry conditions allow it. Only one retry may be in progress at a time. Buyers can start a retry while fewer than 3 retries have been created for the current billing period, counting the store's retries too. subscription_card_update email-link sessions can start retries.

post.description: Charges the next renewal now, ships it when the subscription has delivery, and moves the next billing date forward by one interval. Available while the subscription is active on a Flint-owned billing schedule (billing_schedule_owner is flint), is not set to cancel at the end of its period, is not in a trial, and has no delivery hold or renewal in progress. The subscription's payment method must be active and allow off-session charges. Requires a full buyer session and an idempotency key. Send expected_version to reject concurrent changes. Retry with the same key to recover the same attempt. Returns the subscription, renewal order, and payment attempt, including when the payment is declined. Inspect order_payment_attempt.last_payment_error for a failed payment.

post.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Asks Flint to resume a paused subscription. The request is accepted while the subscription is still paused, with `resume_requested_at` set. Flint then makes it active, or past_due while an overdue period is collected, and sends subscription.resumed. If Flint can't resume it, it stays paused, resume_requested_at clears, and Flint sends subscription.updated. Any other status fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`. To undo a scheduled cancellation, PATCH the subscription with cancel_at_period_end set to false.

post.description: Creates a fresh provider session from a signed launch token after rechecking the authenticated principal, merchant environment, account controller, and component grant. An onboarding session can refresh only sandbox launch tokens created by the same user with an onboarding session. The sandbox is pinned by the launch token, which is the merchant's default sandbox for an onboarding session. Live onboarding requires a live API key or live CLI login, and refresh requires the same credential that created the launch token. A same-key, same-input retry replays the encrypted original result for 24 hours, including its original credentials and expiries. Replay may return an expired credential. Use a new key for a new launch or refresh.

parameters.description: Optional. A retry with the same key and request within 24 hours returns the original result instead of repeating it.

get.description: Returns immutable merchant billing entries for the authenticated merchant environment, newest occurred_at first. Entries in the same second are ordered by type rank, then merchant_billing_entry_id; all three keys are descending. Type ranks are 10 for event_fee, custom_domain, and invoice; 20 for correction; 30 for credit_issued; 40 for credit_applied and credit_refunded; 50 for collection and custom_domain_collection; and 60 for collection_reversal and write_off. An entry can be recorded after entries that occurred later, such as a collection whose bank outcome arrives late. To pick up new entries, filter on created_after. Re-reading the same entry always returns the same values. To export an interval, use merchant_billing_itemized_v1. It fails with data_unavailable when billing projections or membership history are inconsistent, collection outcome or balance transaction evidence is missing, or an entry is invalid. This list does not run the report interval preflights. Default order: occurred_at descending, then the entry type's rank (descending), then merchant_billing_entry_id descending.

parameters.description: Filter by one or more merchant billing entry types. Repeat or comma-separate values. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: type

Issued credit increases available credit without changing the outstanding balance.
Applied credit decreases the outstanding balance and available credit by the same amount.
Refunded credit decreases available credit without changing the outstanding balance.
A collection decreases the outstanding balance without changing available credit.
A collection reversal increases the outstanding balance without changing available credit.
A write-off decreases the outstanding balance without changing available credit.

get.description: Starts a partner app install in the merchant's browser. Flint validates the request, then redirects to Flint's consent screen, where the merchant signs in, chooses a merchant, and approves or denies the requested permissions. Flint then redirects to redirect_uri with code, state, and mode, or with an OAuth error. Request errors found before consent also redirect with an OAuth error once client_id and redirect_uri are validated. Unknown or inactive clients and missing or unregistered redirect URIs return the Flint error envelope. This route takes no credential, and Flint ignores any Authorization header. Flint ignores unrecognized parameters.

post.description: First-party public client flint-cli. Uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded and flat OAuth JSON without a Flint envelope. No client secret or HTTP Basic authentication. Requests are not replayed through idempotency caching. Flint session control extension. Starts device consent bound to the current session and user without consuming the refresh token. Without scope_mode, approval replaces consent; denial or expiry leaves consent unchanged. Redeem using the device_code grant to rotate the latest family token. Set scope_mode=additive and context_id to request additional space-separated scope names for one existing context. Merchant and environment are derived from that context; conflicting hints return invalid_context. Unsupported or environment-disallowed scopes return HTTP 400 invalid_scope; browser denial returns access_denied when polling. Partial approval succeeds and scope in the token response is authoritative. A superseded consent review returns expired_token when its device code is redeemed; start a new review. The existing session remains active.

post.description:
RFC 7009 token revocation for partner apps and flint-cli. Partner apps authenticate with client assertions, HTTP Basic, or client_secret. Assertion rules match the token endpoint. Self-signed private_key_jwt assertions (iss=sub=client_id; ES256, ES384, PS256, RS256, or EdDSA; a single-use jti; exp at most five minutes ahead) are verified against public_key or jwks_url credentials, so sign a fresh one with a new jti for each request. Workload identity assertions have the external issuer as iss and are verified with that issuer's published keys; they use RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384, PS512, ES256, ES384, or ES512, expire no more than one hour and 60 seconds ahead, and need no jti. Revoking a partner refresh token ends its token family, meaning the refresh token and the access tokens issued from it. Revoking a partner access token invalidates every outstanding access token for its environment grant; the refresh token keeps working. Unknown, expired, or other clients' tokens return 200. Revocation doesn't change the install or grant.

For flint-cli, revoking an access or refresh token ends its CLI session and invalidates the session's tokens. The public client sends client_id=flint-cli without a secret or Authorization header. Send application/x-www-form-urlencoded; success has an empty body.

post.description:
Partner apps authenticate with client assertions, HTTP Basic, or client_secret_post. Assertions require client_id, client_assertion_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer, and client_assertion; never mix them with a secret or HTTP Basic. Self-signed private_key_jwt assertions are verified against the app's public_key and jwks_url credentials. They require iss=sub=client_id, a single-string aud equal to the Flint issuer, exp no more than five minutes ahead, and a single-use jti, signed with ES256, ES384, PS256, RS256 (RSA keys of 2048 to 4096 bits and exponent 65537), or EdDSA. Workload identity assertions are tokens from the external issuer of a workload_identity credential: iss is that issuer, and Flint verifies them with the issuer's published keys. They must match the credential's subject, audience, and claim conditions, be signed with RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384, PS512, ES256, ES384, or ES512, and expire no more than one hour and 60 seconds ahead; Flint does not require a jti. Assertion replay storage outages, and JWKS URL or issuer outages that leave no usable keys, return 503 temporarily_unavailable. Partner apps exchange authorization codes with S256 PKCE or rotate refresh tokens for installation-scoped Bearer access tokens. A lost refresh response can be retried for 60 seconds while the replacement remains unused; a replay revokes that environment grant's token family. Authorization codes last 5 minutes and are single use. Partner access tokens last 1 hour; refresh tokens expire 30 days after issuance and rotate on each use. This endpoint follows OAuth token endpoint conventions: send application/x-www-form-urlencoded only. Failures return OAuth token error objects instead of the normal Flint error envelope.

The public client flint-cli supports the RFC 8628 device_code grant and rotating refresh tokens. Pending device requests return authorization_pending; early polling returns slow_down and increases the required interval by five seconds; denial returns access_denied; expired or consumed codes return expired_token. CLI access tokens last 15 minutes. CLI sessions expire after 30 days idle or 90 days total. Reusing a rotated CLI refresh token revokes its family, including when the previous response was lost. A fresh browser login is then required.

With session_mode=contexts at CLI authorization, tokens include oauth_session_id and context_id. CLI refresh requires an explicitly authorized context_id; invalid_context and context_access_denied do not consume the refresh token. Each CLI access token is limited to one context. Ordinary CLI rotation preserves other unexpired access tokens; removing consent immediately invalidates affected tokens. CLI refresh scope may request a subset of the selected grant or context scopes. Only the issued access token is narrowed; consent and other tokens are unchanged. A later refresh without scope restores the full consented scopes. Legacy CLI sessions retain their original response shape. Request rate limits return HTTP 429 temporarily_unavailable with Retry-After and Flint-Rate-Limited-Reason. Device-code token polling returns HTTP 400 slow_down for both early polls and request rate limits.

Workload identities use grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange with subject_token, subject_token_type, and workload_identity_id. subject_token_type must be urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt or urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token. Optional scope narrows the identity scopes for this token; requested_token_type, if supplied, must be urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token. Client authentication, client_id, actor_token, resource, audience, and unrecognized fields are forbidden and return invalid_request. The response includes an opaque fwat_ access token, issued_token_type, workload_identity_id, merchant_id, mode, and sandbox_id in test mode, without a refresh token. The token expires after the shorter of one hour and the remaining subject-token lifetime. Identity deactivation, archive, and scope narrowing take effect on the next API request. Exchange errors use invalid_request, invalid_grant, invalid_scope, unsupported_grant_type, temporarily_unavailable, and server_error. Limits are 300 requests per minute per IP and 600 per minute per identity after signature verification; exceeding either returns HTTP 429 temporarily_unavailable with Retry-After and Flint-Rate-Limited-Reason. No usable external issuer keys returns HTTP 503 temporarily_unavailable.

patch.description: Applies a sparse update to mutable order fields such as customer_id, notes, metadata, tax, the delivery destination, and the requested tip. A request containing only metadata, internal_note, buyer_note, or external_reference_id, with optional expected_version, can update open, closed, paid, and invoice-locked orders without changing totals. Other merchant edits keep hosted and embedded checkout sessions open unless an edit closes or completes the order, which ends the session with order_mutated. Edits can also end invoice, return-resolution, and subscription-plan sessions with order_mutated. A session already past expires_at ends with expired before the edit is applied. These annotation updates are blocked while any order payment attempt remains non-terminal, including an authorization awaiting capture, or checkout payment work is still resolving. Requests combining annotations with other fields use the financial mutation rules for the entire request. Send requested_tip: null to clear the current requested tip. A merchant can correct a paid subscription signup or renewal destination before shipment by sending delivery_destination and the current order version as expected_version. The committed delivery methods must remain eligible, and shipping and tax totals must stay unchanged. When the correction would change the paid totals, the request fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `payment_collected`. The detail can include shipping_money, requoted_shipping_money, tax_money, and requoted_tax_money.

post.description: Creates the link Flint's receipt email carries, to put in buyer email or messages you send yourself. It opens the order in your Flint-hosted customer account without a sign-in, and lets the buyer have the receipt sent again to the order's email. It works for 30 days or 10 opens, whichever comes first; after that the buyer signs in to see the order. The url is a bearer credential. Flint returns it only in this response and in a retry with the same idempotency key, so send it only to the buyer and keep it out of logs. A call with a new key creates another link; earlier links keep working until they expire. When customer_account.mode is merchant_hosted it fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `merchant_hosted_customer_accounts`, and for an order without a customer, with reason `configuration_required`. Send no request body or an empty object ({}). Idempotency is scoped to the merchant, credential, environment, and this resource's route. A replay returns the original link without extending its lifetime or replenishing its opens. Without an idempotency key, each call creates a new link and has no replay result. If Flint cannot retain a result after minting, contact support with the request ID before sending a new request.

get.description: Returns a read-only, human-readable history log for an order. Use it to render timelines and debug what happened, not as a source of truth, ledger, or webhook replacement. Read the owning resource for authoritative state: the order for balances and status, the payment for payment state, the refund for refund outcomes, and the checkout session for checkout state. Do not sum balance_delta_money to compute an order balance. Informational rows such as payment_failed, refund_failed, and checkout_session_expired have a zero balance delta. The default order is newest first. Use sort_direction=asc for chronological timeline rendering. A typical chronological log might show created, payment_failed, payment, refund, then refund_failed; each row gives one reference to click through for the authoritative resource. Default order: created_at descending, then order_activity_id descending.

post.description: Closes an open order and stops further payment. Cancels pending discounts, releases their reservations, and recalculates totals; canceled discounts remain visible with status: "canceled" but no longer reduce the total. Unused order-owned payment intents are canceled. When collected money remains refundable, send collected_money_behavior: keep to close and keep it, or refund it first with POST /v1/refunds and order_id. Closing does not refund money; refunds remain available afterwards. Closing is blocked while payment collection is in progress. To complete a zero-balance order as paid, use POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/pay. closed_reason and closed_at record why and when the order closed. The request body is optional. Send expected_version to reject a mutation based on an outdated order read.

post.description: Creates a fulfillment for the specified quantities on a paid order. Idempotency-Key is required for every request because an inline shipped package can consume inventory. Save the key before sending and retry the same key and body after a lost response. GET /v1/fulfillments supports order_id and external_reference_id filters, but not idempotency_key; an empty list does not prove creation failed. If replay cannot recover the result, contact support with the original key and request ID instead of creating another fulfillment. Use this when you manage fulfillment outside checkout; checkout creates fulfillments for the buyer's delivery selections. While Flint is creating those fulfillments, requests for their quantities return OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS with reason delivery_selection_materializing. Retrieve the order and use its fulfillments. Fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `status_not_reached` when the order is not paid. See the [fulfillment guide](/docs/guides/fulfillment).

patch.description: Updates a single line item on an order. expected_version is the order version returned in data.version. Send gift_card_face_value_money and expected_version to select an unpaid gift card line's face value within its frozen offer and reprice the order before any purchase funding. Send gift_card_recipient and expected_version to replace or clear recipient delivery details before any purchase funding. Checkout credentials can update gift card face value and recipient details together, modifiers, or a line subscription offer selection, each with expected_version. Repeating the current gift card face value does not change the order version. Set subscription to null to buy the line once.

post.description: Starts or resumes a payment attempt on the order. Set action to pay to charge the full outstanding balance, confirm_payment_intents to confirm order-owned payment intents, setup to save a newly collected token on a zero-balance order, or resume to continue an attempt after a pending client action. Each action accepts only its own fields. Only confirm_payment_intents accepts completion_behavior. A pay action without payment_source is valid only when the outstanding balance is zero. To continue a resumable attempt, send action: resume with order_payment_attempt_id and a new Idempotency-Key. An exact retry of the original request with its Idempotency-Key returns the stored response if the request completed, or recovers the same attempt if it was interrupted. Payment intents with manual capture return an active authorization instead of settling immediately. A replay preserves the original HTTP status and domain result. Client authority in order_payment_attempt.pending_actions is available only within 24 hours of the original request and while the matching current payment attempt has status requires_action. Otherwise pending_actions is empty. Read GET /v1/orders/{order_id}/payment-attempts/{order_payment_attempt_id} for the attempt's current state.

409.description: The resource's current state does not allow this action (`ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`). The named resource needs configuration before this action (reason `configuration_required`). The resource does not offer this action or option (reason `not_offered`). The order already collected payment (reason `payment_collected`). Flint can't confirm the payment state automatically and must reconcile it before more money moves (reason `reconciliation_required`). The resource's final status prevents this action (reason `terminal_status`). The resource's current state does not support this action (reason `unsupported_state`). Saving the card needs the buyer's email confirmed in this checkout first (reason `verification_required`). The delivery quote or selection must be replaced (`DELIVERY_REQUOTE_REQUIRED`). A request with the same idempotency key is still in progress (`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_PROGRESS`). The idempotency key was reused with a different request body (`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`). Current eligible inventory cannot satisfy the complete demand (`INVENTORY_INSUFFICIENT`). A count prevents another request of this kind (`LIMIT_REACHED`). The gift card purchase would exceed a daily purchase limit (reason `daily_gift_card_purchases`). The order reached its lifetime limit of payment intents (reason `payment_intents_per_order`). The payment link reached its max_completions (reason `payment_link_completions`). The merchant must complete a readiness step before this operation (`MERCHANT_NOT_READY`). Flint is finishing other work on the resource (`OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS`). A payment attempt is still active (`PAYMENT_ATTEMPT_ACTIVE`). The requested payment option is not available for this merchant, amount, or checkout. The amount_out_of_range reason means the amount is outside this payment option's limits (`PAYMENT_OPTION_UNAVAILABLE`). The hosted payment attempt has too little time left to start a redirect payment (reason `action_window_too_short`). The payment amount is outside this option's accepted range (reason `amount_out_of_range`). ACH debit isn't offered because the order's line items don't show whether the purchase is for goods or services (reason `transaction_purpose_unresolved`). The promotion could not be applied to this order (`PROMOTION_DECLINED`). The promotion has reached its redemption limit (reason `exhausted`). References to this resource prevent the change (`RESOURCE_IN_USE`). The resource changed and the request must be rebuilt from its current state (`VERSION_CONFLICT`).

409.description: The resource's current state does not allow this action (`ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`). Flint can't confirm the payment state automatically and must reconcile it before more money moves (reason `reconciliation_required`). The resource's current state does not support this action (reason `unsupported_state`). A request with the same idempotency key is still in progress (`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_PROGRESS`). The idempotency key was reused with a different request body (`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`). A value is outside the bound the resource's current state allows (`LIMIT_EXCEEDED`). A count prevents another request of this kind (`LIMIT_REACHED`). The order reached its lifetime limit of payment intents (reason `payment_intents_per_order`). The merchant must complete a readiness step before this operation (`MERCHANT_NOT_READY`). The requested payment option is not available for this merchant, amount, or checkout. The amount_out_of_range reason means the amount is outside this payment option's limits (`PAYMENT_OPTION_UNAVAILABLE`). The payment amount is outside this option's accepted range (reason `amount_out_of_range`). ACH debit isn't offered because the order's line items don't show whether the purchase is for goods or services (reason `transaction_purpose_unresolved`). References to this resource prevent the change (`RESOURCE_IN_USE`). The resource changed and the request must be rebuilt from its current state (`VERSION_CONFLICT`).

post.description: Queues a receipt for a paid order, including gift card payments and settled payments, and returns the order unchanged. Send email to choose a recipient, or omit it to use the order's email. Requires Flint-managed receipt delivery. Sending is limited to once every five minutes per order and normalized recipient. Checkout credentials can send only to the address on file. If no address is on file, checkout credentials can send to at most three distinct addresses over the order's lifetime. Receipts sent for this order through this route count toward this limit, including failed deliveries and receipts sent with a secret API key. Merchant callers can choose any address.

post.description: Disconnects a partner app from the authenticated merchant: revokes the install, its environment grants, its refresh tokens and linked API keys, and deletes linked webhook endpoints. Returns current authorized resources, not the recorded response. A pending resource does not prove that the operation succeeded, and an empty list does not prove that it had no effect.

parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20.
parameters.name: page_size

parameters.description: Opaque next_page_token from the previous response. Omit on the first request. You may change `page_size` between pages. Reuse it with the same endpoint, filters, sort, and request context. Do not parse or construct tokens. An invalid, expired, or mismatched token returns a validation error.
parameters.name: page_token

parameters.description: Filter by order ID.
parameters.name: order_id

parameters.description: Filter by customer ID.
parameters.name: customer_id

parameters.description: Filter by invoice ID.
parameters.name: invoice_id

parameters.description: Filter by whether the merchant must capture the payment or respond to a dispute. A dispute requires action when its status is needs_response or inquiry_needs_response, evidence responses are allowed, and its deadline is absent or has not passed. Omit to include both groups.
parameters.name: is_action_required

parameters.description: Filter by payment intent status. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: status

x-enum-descriptions: Waiting for the buyer's payment details. Either nothing has been attempted yet, or the last attempt was declined, failed, or blocked and last_payment_error says why. Confirm again with a new credential.

Payment details are attached, but confirmation hasn't finished. Flint usually confirms in the same request that attaches them, so this status is brief unless that confirmation was interrupted. Resume the order's payment attempt, or call confirm with credential_type attached for a standalone payment intent. The payment_intent.updated event reports changes into this status.

The buyer must finish a step, such as 3D Secure authentication or a redirect, before the payment can continue. The confirm result's current_payment_action describes a standalone payment's step; call confirm with credential_type attached to retrieve it again. Afterward, call confirm with credential_type attached, or resume the order's payment attempt.

Submitted, with the outcome not known yet. ACH debit payments stay here until the bank settles them, which takes a few business days. Card payments pass through briefly. A processing payment intent can't be canceled or updated.
A manual-capture hold is in place and no money has been collected. Capture up to capturable_money, or cancel, before authorization_expires_at.
Canceled before any money was collected, by you or by Flint, for example when an invoice is voided. Final. cancellation_reason says why when Flint knows it. A canceled hold is in released_money.
The payment is collected, and captured_money is the amount. Final.
A manual-capture hold reached authorization_expires_at without a capture, and the funds went back to the buyer. Final. The payment_intent.expired event reports it; cancellation_reason is absent.

parameters.description: Filter by the latest completed risk assessment. Repeat or comma-separate values. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.

x-enum-descriptions: The card processor's fraud screening found nothing unusual.

The screening found strong signs of fraud.

x-enum-descriptions: No dispute is recorded for this payment.
The issuer asked for information before any chargeback. Respond by evidence_due_at.
You responded to the inquiry and the issuer is reviewing it.
The inquiry closed without becoming a chargeback. Final.
A chargeback is open and needs your response by evidence_due_at.
Evidence was submitted and the bank is deciding.
Decided in your favor. Final.
Decided against you, or a bank return that could not be contested. Final.
Resolved before it became a chargeback. Final.
Flint received a dispute state it does not recognize yet. Not final. Treat the dispute as open, do not assume an outcome, and read it again later. A response session still opens.

In processing, succeeded, canceled, or expired it fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `in_progress` or `terminal_status`, with the status in `error.details[].current_status`. amount_money can change only while status is requires_payment_method and before the first confirmation attempt; after that, create a new payment intent. customer_id can change only while status is requires_payment_method, and receipt_email only while it is requires_payment_method or requires_confirmation. Send null to clear tip_money, external_reference_id, receipt_email, or all metadata; amount_money and customer_id cannot be cleared. Order-owned intents accept only metadata and external_reference_id; amount_money, tip_money, customer_id, and receipt_email return INVALID_REQUEST with one NOT_ALLOWED detail per field. This route doesn't attach a payment source: send the buyer's credential to the confirm route.

post.description: Cancels a standalone or order-owned payment intent. Read supported_actions for the actions its stored state accepts. Canceling a hold moves all of capturable_money to released_money, and nothing is charged. A processing payment intent fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `in_progress`; refund a succeeded one instead. Flint derives the owning order payment attempt. A leg held by an active order payment attempt may be refused. Omitted cancellation_reason stays absent. A fresh request for a canceled or expired payment returns ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason already_applied; a same-key retry replays or recovers its original result. A checkout credential can cancel only its own order leg, with requested_by_customer or abandoned when a reason is supplied.

Flint releases the uncaptured remainder in the same request, and a payment intent can be captured only once. amount_money on the payment intent keeps the requested amount; captured_money and released_money record the result. An expired authorization is refreshed before capture and refused with ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED and reason terminal_status or authorization_expired. post.description: Confirms a standalone payment intent. For the first confirmation, send credential_type stripe_confirmation_token, token, or payment_method with its matching credential; a missing credential returns INVALID_REQUEST. After the buyer completes current_payment_action, call this route again with credential_type attached to continue the same payment attempt. Flint confirms again only if the processor still requires it, and otherwise returns the current payment intent. Unverified fee fields are omitted. current_payment_action is null when no buyer action is needed. It can also be null while status is requires_action if Flint cannot produce the action yet; call confirm again with credential_type attached. Order-owned payment intents return 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason order_owned and supported_actions; pay them through POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/pay using remediation.next_actions.

A count prevents another request of this kind (`LIMIT_REACHED`). The merchant's stored images reached the storage quota (reason `image_storage`). The requested payment option is not available for this merchant, amount, or checkout. The amount_out_of_range reason means the amount is outside this payment option's limits (`PAYMENT_OPTION_UNAVAILABLE`).

get.description: Lists payment methods in every status except archived, newest first. Filter by status=active for the cards you can charge. Optionally filter to a customer. Filter by usage off_session to list the payment methods a subscription, automatic invoice, or default payment method can use. Default order: created_at descending, then payment_method_id descending.

parameters.description: Optional Flint customer ID filter.
parameters.name: customer_id

parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20.
parameters.name: page_size

parameters.description: Opaque next_page_token from the previous response. Omit on the first request. You may change `page_size` between pages. Reuse it with the same endpoint, filters, sort, and request context. Do not parse or construct tokens. An invalid, expired, or mismatched token returns a validation error.
parameters.name: page_token

parameters.description: Filter by payment method type. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: type

x-enum-descriptions: A payment card. Its brand, expiry and last four digits are in `card`.

parameters.description: Filter by status. Omitted, the list leaves out archived rows; name archived to include them. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: status

x-enum-descriptions: The only status you can charge, make the default, or attach to a subscription or invoice. An on_session card pays only in checkouts the buyer completes.

Saving has started and isn't confirmed yet: the processor hasn't confirmed the setup, or a buyer who saved the card in checkout with a phone number hasn't confirmed it. Not chargeable. Wait for payment_method.activated.
The card's expiration month has passed. Not chargeable and can't be the default. It returns to active if the expiration date is updated.
Deleted. Readable by ID but never charged again, and left out of lists unless you filter for status=archived. This status is final.

The bank refused the setup, or a phone-number save from checkout wasn't confirmed within 24 hours. Not chargeable. After a refused setup, another attempt with the same client secret can still make it active.

parameters.description: Filter by usage: off_session payment methods can be charged without the buyer; on_session ones were saved by buyers for faster checkout. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: usage

x-enum-descriptions: Saved by the buyer in checkout for faster checkout at this merchant. Flint charges it only in checkouts the buyer completes, and refuses it as a default or for charges made without the buyer.
Can pay subscriptions, automatic invoices, and other charges made without the buyer, and can be a customer's default.

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on created_at.

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on created_at.
parameters.name: created_before

get.description: Lists payment reviews, most recently opened first. A review opens when a `review` rule matches a payment the bank approved. Every status is included unless you filter by `status`. Default order: opened_at descending, then payment_review_id descending.

parameters.description: Filter by review status. Repeat or comma-separate values. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: status

x-enum-descriptions: Waiting for your decision. Approve or decline it.
A decision is being carried out, and the review can't take another; pending_action says which. Wait for payment_review.closed, or payment_review.reopened if a decline's refund fails.
Resolved. closed_reason says how, and closed_by says who. This status is final.

parameters.description: Filter by immutable review risk level. Repeat or comma-separate values. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: risk_level

x-enum-descriptions: The card processor's fraud screening found nothing unusual.
The screening found signs of higher fraud risk.
The screening found strong signs of fraud.
No screening result, for example because Flint blocked the payment before authorization or the payment method isn't screened.

parameters.description: Filter by immutable payment flow. Repeat or comma-separate values. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: payment_flow

parameters.name: payment_intent_id

parameters.description: Filter by Flint order ID.
parameters.name: order_id

parameters.description: Filter by Flint customer ID.
parameters.name: customer_id

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on opened_at.
parameters.name: opened_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on opened_at.
parameters.name: opened_before

parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20.
parameters.name: page_size

parameters.description: Opaque next_page_token from the previous response. Omit on the first request. You may change `page_size` between pages. Reuse it with the same endpoint, filters, sort, and request context. Do not parse or construct tokens. An invalid, expired, or mismatched token returns a validation error.

parameters.description: Include related objects in the response. Supported expansions: customer, order, payment_intent. Include the requested related resources using scoped batch reads for this page. post.description: Declines the payment and closes the review with `closed_reason: declined`. Flint cancels an uncaptured authorization, or refunds the remaining captured amount (captured minus earlier refunds) to the original payment method with reason `fraudulent`. The review is closed once the decline completes. If the refund already failed, the review is `open` again with `last_resolution_failure` set. While the refund is still processing, the decline is accepted but not complete; wait for `payment_review.closed` or `payment_review.reopened`.

parameters.description: Optional 3-letter currency filter.

parameters.description: Optional payout destination type filter. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: type

x-enum-descriptions: Payouts are deposited into a bank account.

parameters.description: Filter by status. Omitted, the list leaves out archived rows; name archived to include them. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: status

x-enum-descriptions: Added and not yet usable.
Ready to receive payouts.
The bank account needs verification before payouts can use it. Complete it in the `payouts` component.
Can't receive payouts. `disabled_reason` says why.
Archived: deleted, and still readable by ID.
The bank rejected a payout to this account. Add a new account or correct this one.

parameters.description: Optional available payout method filter. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: available_payout_methods

parameters.name: default_for_currency

parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20.
parameters.name: page_size

parameters.description: Opaque next_page_token from the previous response. Omit on the first request. You may change `page_size` between pages. parameters.name: page_token
