parameters.description: Filter by the original Idempotency-Key, after trimming surrounding whitespace. Matching is exact and case-sensitive. Returns current authorized resources, not the recorded response. A pending resource does not prove that the operation succeeded, and an empty list does not prove that it had no effect.
parameters.name: idempotency_key

parameters.description: Optional 3-letter currency filter.
parameters.name: currency

parameters.description: Include related objects in the response. Supported expansions: original_payout, payout_destination, reversed_by_payout. Include the requested related resources using scoped batch reads for this page. Each relationship requires its existing target read scopes. Expansion changes the representation without changing pagination tokens. Limits: at most 10 unique expand paths per request.
parameters.name: expand

x-enum-descriptions: Include the full payout object in `original_payout`.
Include the full payout destination object in `payout_destination`.
Include the full payout object in `reversed_by_payout`.

parameters.description: Filter recorded payouts by method. Flint sends only standard payouts. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: method

x-enum-descriptions: Sent using the standard bank transfer method. Every payout Flint sends uses this method.
Sent outside Flint using the processor's instant payout method.
A method Flint does not map.

parameters.description: Optional Flint balance source type filter. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: balance_source_type

x-enum-descriptions: Draws on funds that came from card payments.
Draws on funds that came from bank account payments, such as ACH debits.

parameters.description: Optional payout destination ID filter.
parameters.name: payout_destination_id

parameters.description: Exact-match filter on the caller-owned external reference ID.
parameters.name: external_reference_id

parameters.description: Search across payout ID, external reference ID, description, and statement descriptor. Text fields match any part of the value, and %, _ and \ are ordinary characters, not wildcards. IDs match from the start and need the type prefix, such as po_01.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Optional payout status filter. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: status

x-enum-descriptions: The payout is waiting to be sent.
The payout is on its way to the bank.
The bank accepted the deposit. It can still fail if the bank returns the deposit.
The payout failed and its funds return to the Flint balance.
The payout was canceled before it was sent.

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on created_at.
parameters.name: created_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on created_at.
parameters.name: created_before

parameters.name: arrival_date_from

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on arrival_date at midnight UTC. Use YYYY-MM-DD.
parameters.name: arrival_date_to

post.description: Creates a product, the catalog item buyers purchase through orders, checkout, payment links, and subscriptions. Send `name`, `product_type`, and `variant_mode`. A `simple` product takes one `default_variant`; an `optioned` product takes `options` and `variants`, each variant selecting one value for every option. Price, SKU, and inventory settings live on variants. A SKU or barcode that another variant or bundle already uses fails with `ALREADY_EXISTS`, and a category handle that doesn't exist fails with `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

parameters.description: Flint product ID.
parameters.name: product_id

parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20.
parameters.name: page_size

parameters.description: Opaque next_page_token from the previous response. Omit on the first request. You may change `page_size` between pages. Reuse it with the same endpoint, filters, sort, and request context. Do not parse or construct tokens. An invalid, expired, or mismatched token returns a validation error.
parameters.name: page_token

parameters.description: Filter by status. Omitted, the list leaves out archived rows; name archived to include them. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: status

x-enum-descriptions: Available for use.
Unavailable for use; can be made available again.
Retired from sale and still readable by ID. This status is final.

parameters.description: Byte-sensitive whole-value match on ProductVariant.external_reference_id, preserving whitespace, casing, and Unicode.
parameters.name: external_reference_id

parameters.description: Full-value match on ProductVariant.sku, case- and accent-insensitive, with no trimming. Does not search the inventory item's SKU.
parameters.name: sku

patch.description: Applies a sparse update to a variant: only the fields you send change. A SKU or barcode that another variant or bundle already uses, or an option combination that another variant selects, fails with `ALREADY_EXISTS`. Changes to name, price, SKU, and similar fields apply to new checkouts, links, and plans; existing orders keep what they were charged. Setting the variant inactive, or changing its price currency, fails with `RESOURCE_IN_USE` while an open order, checkout session, active payment link, subscription, subscription plan, or active bundle uses it. Send `expected_version` to reject the update when the variant changed since you read it. Fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `archived` when the resource, or the parent it belongs to, is archived. The error names the archived resource and its `current_status`.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of promotion codes in every status, ordered by created_at descending, then promotion_code_id descending. Archived codes are excluded unless status=archived. Default order: created_at descending, then promotion_code_id descending.

parameters.description: Exact match on the parent promotion ID.
parameters.name: promotion_id

parameters.description: Exact match that ignores case and accents: CAFÉ matches cafe. This is the same rule that makes promotion codes unique. Codes preserve their original spelling. Leading and trailing whitespace are rejected, not trimmed.
parameters.name: code

parameters.description: Filter by status. Omitted, the list leaves out archived rows; name archived to include them. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: status

x-enum-descriptions: Available for use.
Unavailable for use; can be made available again.
Retired from new redemptions and still readable by ID. This status is final.

parameters.description: Filter by whether a code can be redeemed now or why it cannot. available matches available: true; every other value matches unavailable_reason. Values are ORed and ANDed with status. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: availability

parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20.
parameters.name: page_size

parameters.description: Opaque next_page_token from the previous response. Omit on the first request. You may change `page_size` between pages. Reuse it with the same endpoint, filters, sort, and request context. Do not parse or construct tokens. An invalid, expired, or mismatched token returns a validation error.
parameters.name: page_token

parameters.description: Filter by status. Omitted, the list leaves out archived rows; name archived to include them. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: status

x-enum-descriptions: Available for use.
Unavailable for use; can be made available again.
Retired from new redemptions and still readable by ID. This status is final.

parameters.description: Filter by whether a promotion can apply now or why it cannot. available matches available: true; every other value matches unavailable_reason. This filter is ANDed with status. Archived promotions still require status=archived. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: availability

parameters.description: Exact-match filter on the caller-owned external reference ID.
parameters.name: external_reference_id

parameters.description: Search across promotion ID, external reference ID, name, display name, description, and promotion codes. Text fields match any part of the value, and %, _ and \ are ordinary characters, not wildcards. IDs match from the start and need the type prefix, such as promo_01.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Filter to promotions with an explicit product target rule. Universal promotions are not included by catalog target filters.
parameters.name: product_id

parameters.description: Filter to promotions with an explicit variant target rule. Universal promotions are not included by catalog target filters.
parameters.name: variant_id

parameters.description: Filter to promotions with an explicit bundle target rule. Universal promotions are not included by catalog target filters.
parameters.name: bundle_id

parameters.description: Filter to promotions with an explicit category target rule. Universal promotions are not included by catalog target filters.
parameters.name: category_handle

parameters.description: Filter by promotion redemption type. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: redemption_type

parameters.description: Filter by promotion discount class. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: discount_class

parameters.description: Field to sort by. Defaults to created_at; ties are broken by promotion_id.
parameters.name: sort_by

patch.description: Applies a sparse update to promotion fields. application_method, schedule, exclusivity, and combines_with patch by subfield presence. Omitted fields retain stored values; null clears only nullable fields. Sending a different application_method.type replaces the effect while preserving omitted shared settings, including discounted_item_rules. A redeemed promotion can't change its `discount_class` or `application_method` type; the update fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `field_locked`. Archived promotions cannot be changed. Fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `archived` when the resource, or the parent it belongs to, is archived. The error names the archived resource and its `current_status`.

post.description: Creates a refund for an order, a payment intent, a captured gift card redemption, or a gift card load. Set refund_type to full for the full remaining refundable amount, amount for an explicit amount_money, or targets for named line items, charges, and taxes. To refund a gift card redemption made outside a Flint order, set refund_type to amount and send one tender_allocations entry per redemption, with no order_id. A created refund is returned even when processing fails; inspect `status` and `failure_reason`. A same-key replay returns the original refund without another money attempt. This is a financial operation.

post.description: Create or reuse a hosted or embedded checkout session for the buyer's balance on a replacement order linked to this return resolution. The response is `200` when it reuses an existing session and `201` when it creates one. Omit surface to use hosted. The same surface reuses the open session; changing surface replaces an idle session and is refused while a payment is in progress. Use redirects to set where the buyer goes after paying or canceling. The return_url field is an alias for redirects.success_url on hosted checkout or payment_return_url on embedded checkout and must be an address of the merchant's customer account. A reused session takes a new success destination only until a payment starts, then keeps its existing destination.

post.description: Retry a failed resolution. For gift_card_refund_destination_required, send gift_card_refund_destination: new_gift_card to persist the destination before starting the new attempt. The override is accepted for refund, exchange, and corrections of resolutions other than store_credit. A new attempt starts, historical payment and refund IDs stay on the resolution, and a late event from an earlier attempt cannot settle the new attempt. Fails with ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED, with the line's current_status, when a Return line the resolution covers is no longer approved, such as after it was canceled, and with `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` when an approved line no longer has the quantity the resolution covers. Retry is available only when failure_code allows it, and supported_actions includes retry in that case. A failure that retry cannot fix fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`; cancel the resolution instead.

post.description: Creates the link Flint's email about a Return carries, to put in buyer email or messages you send yourself. It opens the Return and its order in your Flint-hosted customer account without a sign-in. Withdrawing the Return needs the buyer to sign in. It works for 30 days or 10 opens, whichever comes first; after that the buyer signs in to see the Return. The url is a bearer credential. Flint returns it only in this response and in a retry with the same idempotency key, so send it only to the buyer and keep it out of logs. A call with a new key creates another link; earlier links keep working until they expire. When customer_account.mode is merchant_hosted it fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `merchant_hosted_customer_accounts`, and for a Return whose order has no customer, with reason `configuration_required`. Send no request body or an empty object ({}). Idempotency is scoped to the merchant, credential, environment, and this resource's route. A replay returns the original link without extending its lifetime or replenishing its opens. Without an idempotency key, each call creates a new link and has no replay result. If Flint cannot retain a result after minting, contact support with the request ID before sending a new request.

post.description: Record one decision for every requested line atomically, then open the Return. To defer a line, decline its quantity or remove it with DELETE /v1/returns/{return_id}/line-items/{return_line_item_id} and open a separate Return for it. Omit completion_mode to use the shared pinned policy mode, or automatic when none sets a mode; disagreeing policies require an explicit completion_mode. completion_blockers reports uncovered approved quantity as resolution_not_selected alongside blockers for unfinished resolutions. Start from each buildable pinned policy proposal or the no-policy defaults, replace every supplied decision field, fill release_timing, and validate the result. When an automatic refund can no longer run through the original payment's provider, the request fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`; send automatic_resolution_type as null to resolve manually, or choose no_monetary_action.

post.description: Record decisions, receipts, inspections, dispositions, and resolutions for an existing requested or open Return in one request. On a requested Return, send one decision for every requested line; missing decisions fail with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `status_not_reached`. Omit completion_mode to use the shared pinned policy mode, or automatic when none sets a mode; disagreeing policies require an explicit completion_mode. On an open Return, omit decision and completion_mode to keep committed values, or send those values unchanged; changed values fail with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `field_locked`. completion_blockers includes resolution_not_selected for any uncovered approved quantity alongside blockers for unfinished resolutions. A line can be processed here only while it has no receipt, inspection, disposition, or resolution. For each line, received_quantity must equal its committed return_required_quantity. Send inspection exactly when the line requires inspection, with acceptance_status accepted. Refunds, payments, replacement orders, and inventory updates complete asynchronously. expected_version is optional and checked only when sent. If the Return has changed since that version, the request fails with VERSION_CONFLICT. When an automatic refund can no longer run through the original payment's provider, the request fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`; send automatic_resolution_type as null to resolve manually, or choose no_monetary_action. Requires an idempotency key and all three scopes: commerce.returns.write, commerce.returns.operations.write, and commerce.returns.resolutions.write.

parameters.description: Exact-match filter after normalization for the parent list's item_type. Accepts 1 through 512 Unicode characters, following the same normalization as item creation. Commas are literal. Values are trimmed and compared exactly after item-type normalization for deduplication and membership. card_fingerprint is the 32-character hexadecimal value from PaymentMethod.fingerprint and is lowercased; case_sensitive_string preserves case and Unicode composition. string and email are lowercased, with accents preserved. email requires a bare address. email_domain is lowercased, has one final dot removed, and converts internationalized domains to ASCII. ip_address uses canonical IP form, including IPv4-mapped IPv6 conversion to IPv4. country uses uppercase ISO codes. card_bin preserves 6 through 8 digits, including leading zeros, and matches the full value. customer_id preserves the validated ID.

post.description: Validates a rule without saving anything. Send mode inline with action and predicate to check a draft; add risk_rule_id to check them as an edit to that rule. Send mode stored_rule with risk_rule_id, and no action or predicate, to check the saved rule as it is. Requires risk.read. Rule content issues produce a preview with `is_valid: false`, every issue in order, `analysis` null, and empty `warnings`. A valid rule returns analysis and any warnings about how the change would affect evaluation. List reference issues are reported at the list_alias path. A new rule at the active-rule limit gets a risk_rule_limit_reached warning. A malformed request fails with `INVALID_REQUEST`, and an unknown `risk_rule_id` fails with `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. Proposing a different action or predicate for a Flint default rule fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `managed_externally`.

Tax is null when no tax address is available; a tax service failure returns 502 EXTERNAL_SERVICE_ERROR. Malformed JSON, unknown fields and request-level problems (a missing or unsupported mode, fields that belong to another mode) return 400. In create mode, every problem with the proposed subscription is returned in errors with is_valid false, not only the first. A preview does not reserve inventory or guarantee a future shipping rate.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of subscriptions for the authenticated merchant. Subscriptions without a next_billing_at never match next_billing_after or next_billing_before, and sort last with sort_by=next_billing_at in either direction. Default order: created_at descending, then subscription_id descending.

parameters.description: Filter by the original Idempotency-Key, after trimming surrounding whitespace. Matching is exact and case-sensitive. Returns current authorized resources, not the recorded response. A pending resource does not prove that the operation succeeded, and an empty list does not prove that it had no effect.
parameters.name: idempotency_key

parameters.description: Filter by where the subscription terms come from: a subscription plan or subscription offers. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: terms_type

x-enum-descriptions: Terms come from the subscription plan in subscription_plan_id.
Terms come from subscription offers; each offer line carries subscription_offer_id. There is no subscription_plan_id.

parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20.
parameters.name: page_size

parameters.description: Opaque next_page_token from the previous response. Omit on the first request. You may change `page_size` between pages. Reuse it with the same endpoint, filters, sort, and request context. Do not parse or construct tokens. An invalid, expired, or mismatched token returns a validation error.
parameters.name: page_token

parameters.description: Filter by subscription status. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: status

x-enum-descriptions: In the free trial. Nothing has been charged.
Current. After a trial it is active while the first charge runs.
Billing is suspended. See pause_reason.
A charge failed and Flint is retrying, or waiting for a new payment method.
Ended. Terminal. This status is final.
The first period's payment is being collected, or is held (see delivery_hold and inventory_wait). Don't provision yet.
Created with a scheduled start. Nothing is charged before starts_at. At starts_at Flint collects the first period; it becomes active once paid, or past_due if the payment fails.

parameters.description: Filter by the system that supplies billing dates. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: billing_schedule_owner

x-enum-descriptions: Flint computes each next billing date and advances it after every paid renewal.
You set each next billing date. Billing waits until you set `next_billing_at`.

parameters.description: Filter external schedules by whether they need another billing date.
parameters.name: awaiting_billing_schedule

parameters.description: When true, returns subscriptions scheduled to cancel at the end of the current period that are not yet canceled. When false, returns every other subscription.
parameters.name: cancel_at_period_end

parameters.description: Filter by Flint customer ID.
parameters.name: customer_id

parameters.description: Filter by the subscription's selected delivery method.
parameters.name: delivery_method_id

parameters.description: Filter by the reason of the current delivery_hold. Does not match upcoming delivery issues. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: hold_reason

x-enum-descriptions: The delivery method was archived or no longer serves the address, and another offered method does.
No offered delivery method serves the address.
The method serves the address but can't be priced, for example a rate callback failure or a variant without `unit_weight`.

parameters.description: Filter by Flint subscription offer ID.
parameters.name: subscription_offer_id

parameters.description: Filter by Flint subscription plan ID.
parameters.name: subscription_plan_id

parameters.description: Exact-match filter on the caller-owned external reference ID.
parameters.name: external_reference_id

parameters.description: Sandbox only. Exact-match filter on `test_clock_id`. A live credential gets `403 FORBIDDEN` with reason `test_mode_required`.
parameters.name: test_clock_id

parameters.description: Search across subscription ID, external reference ID, customer, and plan. Text fields match any part of the value, and %, _ and \ are ordinary characters, not wildcards. IDs match from the start and need the type prefix, such as sub_01.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Field to sort by. Defaults to created_at; ties are broken by subscription_id.
parameters.name: sort_by

x-enum-descriptions: When the resource was created.
When the resource was last updated.
When the subscription is next due to bill.

parameters.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc.
parameters.name: sort_direction

x-enum-descriptions: Orders results from the lowest sort value to the highest.
Orders results from the highest sort value to the lowest.

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on created_at.
parameters.name: created_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on created_at.
parameters.name: created_before

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on updated_at.
parameters.name: updated_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on updated_at.
parameters.name: updated_before

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on next_billing_at.
parameters.name: next_billing_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on next_billing_at.
parameters.name: next_billing_before

parameters.description: True matches subscriptions with a delivery hold, an upcoming delivery hold, an inventory wait, or a delivery-action-required pause, plus past_due subscriptions and active or incomplete subscriptions whose billing date passed more than 24 hours ago without payment. False is the exact complement. Other filters still apply.

parameters.description: Include related objects in the response. Supported expansions: customer, payment_method, subscription_plan. post.description: Creates a subscription for a customer outside checkout. Send `customer_id`, the `terms` (a subscription plan or subscription offers), and `billing_start`, which says whether billing begins now, on a later date, or continues a period the buyer already paid elsewhere. Renewals charge `payment_method_id`, or the customer's default payment method when you omit it; with neither, the request fails with `INVALID_REQUEST` naming `payment_method_id`. The payment method must belong to the customer, be active, and allow charges without the buyer present. A plan that is not active fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`.

post.description: Creates a link to one subscription in your Flint-hosted customer account, to put in buyer email or messages you send yourself. Omit purpose or send subscription_view for read-only access without a sign-in. Send subscription_manage to also let the buyer cancel, pause, or undo a scheduled cancellation, subject to your store's policy and the subscription's state. subscription_manage requires commerce.subscriptions.write; subscription_view requires commerce.subscriptions.read. Neither purpose permits other subscription changes or access to another subscription. Both work for 14 days or 5 opens, whichever comes first; after that the buyer signs in. The url is a bearer credential. Flint returns it only in this response and in a retry with the same idempotency key, so send it only to the buyer and keep it out of logs. A call with a new key creates another link; earlier links keep working until they expire. When customer_account.mode is merchant_hosted it fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `merchant_hosted_customer_accounts`. Send no request body, an empty object ({}), or an optional purpose. Idempotency is scoped to the merchant, credential, environment, and this resource's route. A replay returns the original link without extending its lifetime or replenishing its opens. Without an idempotency key, each call creates a new link and has no replay result. If Flint cannot retain a result after minting, contact support with the request ID before sending a new request.

post.description: Cancels a subscription and records who asked, why, and when in cancellation_details. With cancel_immediately: true it ends now. Otherwise, trialing ends at trial_end_at, active at current_period_end_at (or now when a renewal delivery hold has expired), and past_due at next_retry_at instead of that retry. Scheduled, incomplete, paused, and past_due without next_retry_at require cancel_immediately: true or fail with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `period_end_unavailable`. Read scheduled_cancel_at for the scheduled end time. A buyer's cancellation follows the store's customer_account.buyer_capabilities. Send expected_version to reject a concurrent change.

post.description: Replaces the subscription's lines and recurring options with the active target plan's current terms. Paired lines keep their quantities unless line_items overrides them. Pair by the same plan line on the same plan, then variant or bundle, then the only line on each side. Unpaired target lines use their plan quantity. If an adjusted current line cannot be paired, send quantities for every target line; otherwise the request fails with quantity_not_carried before any change. With billing_starts next_renewal, changes terms now without charging and keeps the current period and next billing date. With billing_starts now, charges a new period and credits unused paid item time after promotions; the plan changes only when payment succeeds. If the credit exceeds the new item charge, choose next_renewal. Omit interval and quantity to keep their current values; the target plan must offer them. Contract terms and existing recurring promotions are preserved. Requires Idempotency-Key; retry with the same key to recover the same result. Returns status 200 for a decline, with a closed unpaid order, failed order_payment_attempt, and unchanged subscription. Inspect order_payment_attempt.last_payment_error and update the subscription payment method before trying again. Send expected_version to reject a concurrent change. After a confirmed CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION with billing_starts now, refresh the subscription and send a new Idempotency-Key. The buyer account cannot change plans.

post.description: Charges the next renewal now, ships it when the subscription has delivery, and moves the next billing date forward by one interval. Available while the subscription is active on a Flint-owned billing schedule (billing_schedule_owner is flint), is not set to cancel at the end of its period, is not in a trial, and has no delivery hold or renewal in progress. The subscription's payment method must be active and allow off-session charges. Requires an idempotency key; retry with the same key to recover the same attempt. Returns the subscription, renewal order, and payment attempt, including when the payment is declined. Inspect order_payment_attempt.last_payment_error for a failed payment.

post.description: Records the seller's attestation and creates or completes the tax account from verified business details and the default line-item tax category in settings. Syncs registrations and removes tax-account copies of deleted registrations. Reconnect retains the tax account and does not turn the default tax setting back on. A rejected stored registration returns attention_required with registration_rejected. Successful configuration marks open calculated automatic-tax orders without an issued invoice incomplete and advances their versions. A same-key retry resumes setup without creating another account; unconfirmed account creation requires support. Retrieve the connection after a lost response.

post.description: Turns automatic tax off while retaining the tax account and registrations for reconnecting. Choose tax_default_behavior explicitly: turn_off stops adding tax to new orders, checkout sessions and renewals that inherit the default; keep leaves the default unchanged, refuses those orders and holds renewals for retry without charging buyers or starting dunning. Payment links that explicitly enable automatic tax are refused when creating a checkout session with either choice. Settings are updated first when needed, then the connection is disconnected and open calculated automatic-tax orders without an issued invoice snapshot become incomplete. Issued invoice snapshots are unchanged. A same-key retry resumes after settings were changed; after a lost response, retrieve the connection and disconnect again if needed.

parameters.description: Optional. A retry with the same key and request within 24 hours returns the original result instead of repeating it.

statements.text: I confirm this Flint merchant represents one independently liable legal seller and taxpayer. It does not share registrations with another seller, switch sellers by transaction, or use Flint as Merchant of Record.
I authorize Flint to create and configure a Quaderno account for automatic tax calculations. Flint does not file returns or remit tax through this connection.
Automatic tax costs 0.5% of each payment where Flint calculates tax above zero. Payments with tax you supply, or with no tax, have no automatic tax fee.

post.description: Saves one US state registration for a non-overlapping, inclusive date window. Start_date may be up to 365 days ahead; end_date is optional. Before the connection is active, saves locally as pending without creating a tax account. On an active connection, syncs the registration in this request. Acceptance of a registration effective today marks open calculated automatic-tax orders without an issued invoice incomplete, advancing their versions. Scheduled registrations do not invalidate calculations. A definitive rejection before a tax-account registration exists removes the pending registration and leaves working tax and orders unchanged. If a tax-account copy exists or may have been created, rejection cleanup marks those open orders incomplete and advances their versions. Successful cleanup leaves the connection active. An uncertain outcome keeps the registration pending and the connection active; retry with the same key to resume without duplicating the registration. If the key is lost, filter the list by state and match the submitted start_date, delete the pending registration and create again after deletion succeeds.

delete.description: Hard-deletes a pending, rejected or scheduled registration and returns its final snapshot with status removed. While disconnected, deletes locally and records tax-account cleanup for the next connect. Otherwise, removes a possible tax-account copy first. If earlier creation is unconfirmed, an empty tax-account registration list does not prove the copy is absent: EXTERNAL_SERVICE_ERROR keeps the local registration. Retry the same request with the same idempotency key until the copy can be identified and removed. Provider failure retains the local registration. An online deletion of a pending or rejected registration that removes existing or possibly created tax-account coverage marks open calculated automatic-tax orders without an issued invoice incomplete and advances their versions. Scheduled and disconnected deletions do not invalidate calculations. Scheduled deletion removes its tax-account copy immediately unless disconnected, without pausing automatic tax or invalidating calculations. Active and ended registrations cannot be deleted. A later GET fails with `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

patch.description: Updates locally without a tax-account call. Pending and rejected registrations allow registration_number, start_date and end_date; registration_number and start_date require a connection that is not active. Scheduled and active registrations allow only end_date. A pending or rejected registration whose tax-account copy exists or may have been created cannot change start_date; delete it and create it again. Ended registrations cannot be changed. End_date must be on or after start_date and today (UTC); null clears it before the registration ends. Date windows in the same state cannot overlap. To replace an active registration number, set its end_date, then create a replacement starting the next day. Changing end_date does not invalidate calculations made today. An empty patch is invalid.

x-enum-descriptions: Stopped at `frozen_at`. You can advance it and create customers on it.

Flint is moving the clock's customers and their subscriptions to `frozen_at`, running the billing that falls due along the way, in order. Resources on the clock can show any time between the previous `frozen_at` and this one until the clock is `ready`. Wait for `test_clock.ready`, or read the clock until its status changes.
Flint couldn't finish an advance. Resources on the clock may have processed only part of it. The clock can't advance again: archive it and create a new one.
Archived with `DELETE`. The clock stays readable but never advances, and no new customer can be created on it. Its customers and subscriptions stay at `frozen_at`. This status is final.

patch.description: Updates a webhook endpoint's URL, description, status, subscribed events, event sources, signing methods, or pinned API version. Only the fields you send change. Sending `enabled_events`, `event_sources`, `installed_merchant_modes`, or `signing_methods` replaces that whole list and requires `expected_version`; a stale version fails with `VERSION_CONFLICT`. Adding `hmac` when no secret exists issues the first secret and returns it once. Removing `hmac` deletes all shared secrets. Partner-source endpoints are global configuration. Changes to them or their events and deliveries require a live-mode credential or a Dashboard session, including test events and endpoints subscribed only to test installed-merchant events. get.description: Returns recent canonical webhook events for the authenticated merchant. Sandbox reads omit global partner-source records. Filters selecting only partner_app or installed_merchants return an empty collection. Direct resource reads of partner-source records return 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND in sandbox mode; exact-ID list filters return an empty collection when no visible records match. Default order: created_at descending, then webhook_event_id descending.

An immutable gift card financial movement was posted. Corrections create new transactions.

An inventory level version advanced.

An invoice was created.
An invoice balance closed with positive applied credit and no positive net collection.
A scheduled invoice could not be issued and remains a draft.
An invoice was issued and became open for collection.
A late fee was added to an invoice balance.
An invoice reached a configured late fee date.
The unpaid remainder of an invoice late fee was waived.
An invoice's outstanding balance was written off as uncollectible.
An invoice passed its payment due date with an outstanding balance.
An invoice balance closed with positive net collection. Collection, allocated credit, waived fees, or reversal recovery can clear the balance.
An invoice became partially paid or received another collection while a balance remained. Sent for online, gift card, and manual payments.
Part of an invoice's payment was refunded.
An invoice's payment was fully refunded.
An invoice reminder is ready to send.
An invoice balance reopened after a payment or credit allocation was reversed. The invoice is open or partially paid.
An invoice was sent to the customer.
An invoice draft, schedule, reminder settings, refund state, or other non-status detail was updated.
An invoice was voided and can no longer be paid.
An invoice email delivery attempt failed.

An order was created.
An order has an inventory failure that requires operator action.
An order inventory exception was resolved.

An order became fully refunded.

A payment intent was created.

A payment attempt failed.
A payment was submitted and is awaiting its final outcome.
The payment requires a customer action such as 3D Secure authentication.
The payment was authorized and is awaiting capture.
A payment intent succeeded.
A payment intent changed without entering a more specific lifecycle status.
A payment link was created.
A payment link changed, including being activated or deactivated. Sales through the link don't send this event.
A payment method became active and can be charged.
A saved payment method was deleted. It stays readable and can't be charged again.
Saving a payment method failed.
A payment review was resolved or closed by a payment lifecycle change.
A payment was placed into manual review.
A declined review's refund failed, so the review is open again and needs a decision.
A payout to the merchant's bank was canceled.
A payout to the merchant's bank was created.
A payout failed and funds were returned to the balance.
A completed payout was reversed.
A payout arrived at the merchant's bank.
A payout changed state.
A payout destination was removed. It stays readable by ID with status archived.
A payout destination (bank account) was added.
A payout destination was disabled.
A payout destination was updated.
The merchant's payout schedule or settings changed.
A product was archived. Its variants were archived with it and send no events of their own.
A product was created. Each variant it created sends product_variant.created.

A product's own fields, options, images, categories or modifier set changed. Variant changes send product_variant events instead, although they also change the product's rollups and version. Rollups (default_variant, price_range, active_variant_count, variant_count, available_for_sale and delivery_configuration_status) and copied category names and handles send no product events. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A variant was archived on its own. Archiving its product sends only product.archived.
A product variant was created.

A product variant was updated. Copied selected option names and values, available_for_sale, effective_images and delivery readiness send no variant events. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A promotion was archived. Its codes were archived with it and send no events of their own.
A promotion was created. Each code it created sends promotion_code.created.

A promotion was updated. Changes to codes_summary, uses_count, available and unavailable_reason, including redemptions and schedule boundaries, send no promotion events. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A promotion code was archived on its own. Archiving its promotion sends only promotion.archived.
A promotion code was created.

A promotion code was updated. Changes to uses_count, available and unavailable_reason, including redemptions and schedule boundaries, send no promotion code events. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A refund was created.
A refund failed.
A refund partially succeeded.
A refund succeeded in full.
A refund changed without entering a more specific lifecycle status.
An asynchronous report reached a terminal generation failure.
An asynchronous report completed and its authenticated CSV download is ready.
A Return was canceled.
A Return completed after every required merchandise and buyer-value obligation cleared.
A Return was created.
The merchant or policy automation recorded line-level Return decisions.
A completed Return was reopened for additional work.
A Return or one of its line-level progress projections changed.
A merchandise disposition was recorded for a Return.
A Return disposition changed execution state.
Acceptance was decided for a Return inspection observation.
A Return inspection observation was recorded.
A Return inspection observation was superseded by an auditable correction.
A Return receipt observation was recorded.
A Return receipt observation was superseded by an auditable correction.
An unmatched Return receipt line was verified against the expected merchandise.
A proposed buyer-value resolution was created for a Return.
A Return resolution changed proposal, gate, effect, or fulfillment state.
A shipment was created.
A shipment changed, including status, details, or package count.
A subscription's first paid period was collected, or it was created already paid or imported, so it is active. Sent once per subscription.
A subscription was canceled.
A subscription was set to cancel at the end of its billing period or trial, or in place of its next payment retry. `scheduled_cancel_at` says when.
A subscription was created.
A subscription billing cycle was skipped without a charge.
A subscription renewal needs an address, method, or rate correction before it can be charged.
A subscription delivery hold is approaching its pause date.
A subscription's delivery preference changed. Paid, unshipped renewals keep their existing destination.
A subscription used its automatic payment retry budget.
A subscription renewal failed and is past due.
A subscription was paused.
A subscription billing attempt succeeded.
A subscription moved to another plan, or to its plan's current lines and prices. When the change bills a new period, subscription.payment_succeeded is sent with it.
A subscription's scheduled cancellation was undone, so it renews as usual.
A subscription renewal is approaching.
A paused subscription was resumed.
A subscription trial is approaching its end.
A subscription changed and no more specific subscription event describes the change.
A subscription delivery method migration finished. Its counts and failures identify which subscriptions moved.
A subscription payment retry was created.
A subscription payment retry failed.
A subscription payment retry succeeded.

The automatic tax connection's public state changed, including setup, support disable, or a registration change. Read-time business-detail changes and provider pauses send no event; read the connection again when automatic tax fails.
A sandbox test clock started advancing to its new frozen_at.
A sandbox test clock was archived.
A sandbox test clock was created.
A sandbox test clock couldn't finish advancing. Resources on the clock may have processed only part of the advance. Flint records test_clock.failed after every event the advance caused.

A sandbox test clock finished advancing. Flint records test_clock.ready after every event the advance caused. Deliveries can still arrive in any order; GET /v1/webhook-events lists them all once the clock is ready.

get.description: Streams canonical merchant webhook events created after the connection opens or after the supplied event ID. SSE event IDs are resumable webhook event IDs. Control records include ready, gap, withheld, and disconnect. Gap records indicate cursor_unavailable or payload_expired; withheld records hide payloads the caller cannot read. Backpressure emits disconnect with reason backpressure and resume_cursor identifying the last sent event, so clients can reconnect without losing events.

parameters.description: Filter by canonical merchant webhook event type. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: event_type

statements.text: I confirm this Flint merchant represents one independently liable legal seller and taxpayer. It does not share registrations with another seller, switch sellers by transaction, or use Flint as Merchant of Record.
I authorize Flint to create and configure a Quaderno account for automatic tax calculations. Flint does not file returns or remit tax through this connection.
Automatic tax costs 0.5% of each payment where Flint calculates tax above zero. Payments with tax you supply, or with no tax, have no automatic tax fee.

releases.overview: Balance transactions report fee charges as positive amounts (on a payment, the processing fee plus any add-on fees), name their timestamp `occurred_at`, and name the related resource in `related_resource` with `resource_type` and `resource_id`. Tax categories split into `line_item_tax_category` for items and `charge_tax_category` for charges, so the field name tells you which set of values applies.

changes.summary: Balance transaction fee charges are positive and fee credits are negative.
changes.action: Read a positive `fee_money` as a fee charged and a negative one as a fee returned. `net_money` is unchanged.

changes.summary: Balance transactions name their related resource in `related_resource`, with `resource_type` and `resource_id`.
Balance transactions use occurred_at for the transaction timestamp.
Tax categories use line_item_tax_category for items and charge_tax_category for charges.
changes.action: Replace `tax_category` with `line_item_tax_category` on product variants, modifiers, bundles, and line item taxes, and with `charge_tax_category` on delivery methods and charge taxes.
